#1216. Pastore previews PSG vs. Roma: ‘Gasperini’s philosophy is clear, like Luis Enrique’

Former Roma and Paris Saint-Germain attacker Javier Pastore has shared his thoughts ahead of the meeting of his two former clubs in the Champions League on Wednesday evening, and has explained what makes the two teams so enjoyable to watch: ‘Gasperini has made his philosophy clear to the players, like Lucho at PSG’.

Roma face another tough test in the Champions League away against the reigning champions, PSG, on Wednesday night. The Giallorossi have four points from their opening four matches in the competition this season after tests away against Fenerbahce and Manchester United and at home against Slovan Bratislava and Real Madrid.

PSG, meanwhile, have had a perfect start and will be looking to make it five wins from five on Wednesday night. Luis Enrique’s side have beaten Slovan Bratislava, Manchester City, Barcelona and Villarreal already this season.

“Both play to impose themselves with great talents in attack,” said Pastore in an interview with La Gazzetta dello Sport. “They have coaches who work differently, but with the same attacking and counter-attacking principles. PSG will be more confident and have a perfect record, Roma need to pick up points. It will be an exciting game.”

Pastore feels that the coaches might be both sides’ strongest assets.

“Both know how to get into their players’ heads. They are not just good tactically, but also at managing their teams, which is fundamental in modern football. I don’t know Gasperini very well, but he did great things at Atalanta and he’s brought an offensive, selfless style of play to Roma. They take risks and have lots of quality going forwards.

“He’s made his philosophy clear to the players, like Lucho at PSG, where he has changed the game concepts and the players’ mentality, who still follow him after winning two Champions Leagues.”

Pastore pinpointed the players that Roma should be wary of.

“I’ve always liked Doue and Kvaratskhelia, who won’t be involved unfortunately, but also Mendes and Hakimi, the best full-backs in the world. I also like everything about Neves, a very special player who doesn’t always draw attention, but always helps his team in recovery, building from the back, creating space, looking for smart passes and arriving in front of goal. He’s a complete player.”

“For Roma, Dybala is a spectacle, dangerous anywhere. Malen is better than any other striker this year. And there’s also Soule, who brings something different, is technical and dribbles and scores well.”

Alarmingly for Roma, Pastore says that there are no weaknesses in the PSG side.

“I don’t see any, but maybe they will come out while the game is in progress. PSG are a united team built on the consistency of their play both in attack and defence. And Gasperini is following a similar path with Roma, always wanting to score one more than the opponent. You could even see it against Real Madrid, despite the result.”

Still, Malen’s form is encouraging. The Dutchman has scored 16 goals from 15 games across all competitions and netted four goals during Roma’s 5-1 win over Parma on Sunday.

“With Malen in this type of form, pretty much any ball into the box ends with a goal and it’s hard to stop him. Dybala is dangerous in every situation: From free-kicks, from the edge of the area, with an assist or a shot into the top corner. These are the types of players who usually give you something extra in games like this.”

And lastly, when asked if he had to pick a side, Pastore said: “Rome is beautiful with wonderful people, a place I lived for three great years. I’m in Paris more often because I got married there, and my children were born there. But I would take the Italian food anywhere.”

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

Screw Pastore, disgusting person. He robbed Roma and Elche, collecting wages KNOWING full well his career and knees were done. A real piece of work.

Liverpool are facing renewed interest from Bayern Munich in Florian Wirtz and Rio Ngumoha as the German giants prepare for the possibility of losing Michael Olise or Jamal Musiala.

Bayern are assessing several attacking options across Europe, with Manchester City winger Jérémy Doku also featuring on their shortlist.

However, convincing Liverpool to part with two players who could have an enormous influence on the club’s future under Andoni Iraola will be particularly difficult.

According to TEAMtalk, Bayern are maintaining a strong interest in Wirtz and Ngumoha as uncertainty surrounds the futures of Olise and Musiala.

The German champions have yet to finalise a contract extension with Olise, who has attracted interest from Real Madrid and Barcelona.

Bayern’s admiration for Wirtz dates back to his Bayer Leverkusen days, while Ngumoha’s rapid development has caught the attention of their recruitment department.

Both Liverpool players scored and provided an assist during Sunday’s impressive 4-0 victory over Manchester United.

However, Bayern’s chances of signing Ngumoha could soon suffer a significant setback.

A recent CaughtOffside report revealed that Liverpool are close to finalising a new long-term contract for the 18-year-old winger amid growing interest from European heavyweights.

Bayern are also monitoring Doku, despite the Belgian international signing a contract extension with Manchester City until 2031 earlier this year.

Liverpool should firmly resist any approach for either player.

Wirtz is beginning to demonstrate why the Reds invested so heavily in bringing him to Anfield, with Iraola seemingly helping the German international rediscover his confidence and attacking influence.

Ngumoha, meanwhile, represents exactly the type of emerging talent Liverpool should be building around rather than cashing in on.

The teenager’s fearless approach, explosive acceleration and ability to unsettle defenders make him an exciting long-term prospect.

Bayern’s interest is understandable, but their recruitment problems should not become Liverpool’s concern.

Securing Ngumoha to an improved contract and continuing to build the attack around Wirtz should be straightforward priorities for the Anfield hierarchy.

At 18 and 23 respectively, the pair could potentially form the foundation of Liverpool’s attack for much of the next decade.

Selling either player would undermine that vision, regardless of how financially attractive Bayern’s eventual proposals might be.

#1214. Fleetwood knock out Arsenal in one of biggest shocks in League Cup history

Leaving Highbury was a wrench for Arsenal in 2006, but it was not the case 20 years later. They could not wait to get out of the stadium with the same name after a night that left Mikel Arteta looking haunted.

Fleetwood Town did not have any marble halls; they did not even have enough space in their car park for the three coaches carrying Arsenal’s entourage, but they have a proud tradition, spirit and, as a result, they will dine out on a result that will be celebrated for months and talked about for decades.

Eighty-four rungs separated these teams at kick-off, but, now and again, you get a situation when the floodlights are on, belief is high and the sense of history is prevalent. It is an intoxicating combination and, gloriously, the stars aligned. Mission impossible was completed.

Having chiselled out a 1-1 draw in 90 minutes in which Max Dowman was sent off, Fleetwood dispatched five nerveless spot-kicks, the last one thundered in by Conor Haughey after Bruno Guimarães’s penalty was saved by Jay Lynch.

“You have got to have confidence, haven’t you?” Haughey asked. “I just thought, I’m going to run up and smack it. It’s incredible. I come from Belfast and if you don’t have confidence, you will get eaten up.”

This was ignominious for Arsenal, an elimination from this tournament to rival the 1969 loss in the final to Swindon Town or the 2012 exit to Bradford, then also of League Two. What made this so astonishing was the fact that Mikel Arteta went so strong.

You should never be surprised by anything these days, but, even still, an eight-minute delay because of a drone flying over this wonderful little venue would not have been on anyone’s bingo card. Only 57 seconds had been played when Michael Salisbury, the referee, saw a light in the sky and said “stop”.

A drone stops play at the Highbury Stadium. https://t.co/TvjNjjACFM

The precaution was understandable. Only 10 days ago, one idiot escaped from a village to kick a rugby ball off the roof of an apartment block into the Gtech Community Stadium while Brentford and Liverpool were playing and could have caused serious injury.

So while the locals harrumphed as the players tried to keep themselves warm, no risk could be taken. Eventually, police apprehended the operator in a nearby park. It was something unfathomable, which was also true of what happened when the contest resumed.

The anticipation was that Arsenal would saunter clear against opponents who had lost at Exeter City on Saturday, leaving them 18th in England’s fourth tier. But it only took a few skirmishes to appreciate this was not going to be the cakewalk anticipated in what was the biggest occasion in Fleetwood’s history.

Arteta absolutely knew his team were not operating at the levels they should have been. He was wrapped up against the elements in a thick black jacket but, every so often, he would express his exasperation at Jurriën Timber, captain for the night, to “get forward!”

They were in a battle, that much was obvious, and one challenge from Shaun Rooney – so forceful you thought the ball might burst – sent Myles Lewis-Skelly spinning like a top. How Fleetwood’s fans loved it, roaring their approval as the young England international hit the ground with a thump.

Arsenal had one good chance when Dowman skipped down the right and dragged a shot across the box that Viktor Gyökeres could not divert but then, wonderfully, things took a totally unexpected turn when Fleetwood poked their noses in front.

It was a League Two goal in its simplicity, but that is no criticism. Harrison Neal helped a long ball forward, putting it behind Marli Salmon and Aaron Loupalo-Bi relished the chance to get into a foot race, grappling with the England Under-17 international.

Salmon looked like he had him at one point, but Loupalo-Bi was strong – not to mention composed – and he held off the challenge to slide a left-footed shot through the legs of Illan Meslier, who was making his Arsenal debut. What followed was unique to the magic of an English cup tie.

FLEETWOOD TAKE THE LEAD! 😱 Loupalo-Bi puts League Two side Fleetwood ahead against Arsenal 💥 https://t.co/zTFEkCp0oL

As the home fans set off flares, filling the air with plumes of thick, red smoke, the theme tune to Captain Pugwash was played. Arteta tried to find answers from his coaching staff, amid the cacophony, but occasionally you do not have to look too deep for answers.

Could the miracle happen? When half-time arrived with Fleetwood still in the lead, you began to wonder. But then you saw Ben White and Martin Odegaard go through intense warm-ups so they could be introduced at the start of the second half and you knew the mountain had become taller.

So it proved. Odegaard, with his mesmerising left foot and all-encompassing vision, did more in the first five minutes of the second period than many of his colleagues had managed before the interval, and Arsenal levelled in that initial flurry through Gyökeres’s first domestic goal of the campaign.

Viktor Gyökeres gets his first goal of the season and Arsenal are level against Fleetwood! 🔴 https://t.co/LfZcIbAfCX

A game of attack against defence played out for the remainder before Dowman was harshly dismissed in the 85th minute after reacting to a tough challenge from Neal. There was still time for Fleetwood’s Lynch to make two excellent saves from White and Odegaard in added time as Arsenal tried to avoid the shoot-out lottery. They could not and how it hurt them.

HUGE save from Jay Lynch! https://t.co/dLJaFwCmHQ

“Football’s getting a little bit more, I don’t know, clinical and removed,” Matt Lawlor, the Fleetwood manager, said. “To me, there was that feeling we all get as football fans. That was what you kind of live for, isn’t it? To be a part of it is special.

“To be giving that to football fans and especially Fleetwood fans is unbelievably special. I’m really proud of it. Football’s a funny old game, isn’t it?”

First of all, congratulations to Fleetwood for going through in the next round, in the manner they’ve done it, the atmosphere they have created, and, yeah, a really sad day for us.

I cannot fault at all the attitude of the players. I haven’t seen anyone not doing what is required at this level. But, obviously, we insisted so much, we have so much of the ball, so many chances, so many shots, and if you want the margins to be bigger than going to the penalties, obviously, you need to capitalise on that. And we didn’t. And football is about that.

Attitude wise, absolutely zero [wrong] otherwise, I would be here absolutely fuming. I’m sad, I think we are all sad. We have a massive responsibility to carry this badge in the best possible way. It had nothing to do with effort or application or determination to win it, but we lack other things to, to create a much bigger margin than today, with what we produce, they really should have been shown in the scoreline.

Something that we discussed already before the match.

It’s difficult to see on the cameras, I prefer to watch it back properly and I will assess the situation.

We will learn from everything [on if he will learn from it].

I don’t think it will [sink in], it’s really hard to address the players when we have a league game on Saturday and I didn’t want to be the bearer of reality. The biggest night in the club’s history. We’ve beaten the champions, somehow!

We knew before the game, we’re not stupid enough and not egotistical enough that you think we’re going to go to the best team in the country and the most organised team in the country and the best of the basics and the world-class players, in that we’re going to go and outplay them. So we had to ride our luck, we had to deny space, we had to deny options for them. And I think we did that really, really well in terms of the majority of the game.

Obviously, the goal happens, but they’re going to happen; they’re so good at football. The footballers that they have, the gaps that they find and we see it every week in the Premier League.

To beat the English champions on penalties, credit to everyone one of these lads. We looked at Grimsby beating Man Utd last year. We compared it even though these are the champions. We thought ‘if we lay it all out there, let’s see what happens.

The team who are 18th in League Two have beaten the Premier League champions. Nine perfect penalties and one miss from Bruno Guimaraes.

Lynch dives to his left after the Guimaraes stutter, good save from the goalkeeper.

Arsenal are out if Haughey converts this penalty.

Cannon scores against Arsenal at Highbury. Bruno G up next.

Gyokeres finishes with power. The perfect record continues. Cannon up next for Fleetwood.

Meslier dives the wrong way again, Davies does well to keep his composure after needing a few attempts to spot the ball.

All four penalties have been scored, Havertz sends Lynch the wrong way after missing a few chances in regulation time.

Cracking penalty from midfielder, into the roof of the net with power.

Lynch guessed the right way, but Odegaard found the bottom-right corner with power.

He waits for Meslier to dive and rolls the ball into the opposite corner.

Odegaard is going to take first for Arsenal.

Their striker Coughlan, on as a sub in the second half, is going to take the first penalty of the shoot-out against Meslier.

Arsenal taken to penalties by the team 18th in League Two. They finish the game with a sense of injustice after Max Dowman’s red card, but they only have themselves to blame for not putting Fleetwood to the sword in the second half. Huge defensive effort from the underdogs.

Arsenal continue to pile the pressure on even with 10 men, but Guimaraes’s cross is claimed by Lynch.

Fleetwood then go on the attack, and White makes a mess of Rooney’s cross, conceding a cheap corner.

One last chance to win the tie, but Arsenal deal with it.

Havertz then heads the ball down in a dangerous zone but no Arsenal player is there. Arsenal have had their best spell since the red card, almost playing with some anger.

Brilliant save from Lynch to deny Ben White at the back post! Stopped right on the line, just as five minutes of stoppage time are shown on the board.

Then Lynch turns behind another Odegaard shot for a corner.

HUGE save from Jay Lynch! https://t.co/dLJaFwCmHQ

Bruno Guimaraes floats in a cross that is too heavy for Ben White. Fleetwood have a free-kick which they are going to send into the mixer but Arsenal clear.

Mikel Arteta did not have much sympathy for Dowman as he walked past him, but replays suggest it was a harsh call. No VAR in play tonight. Arsenal now playing with 10 for the final minutes.

I suspect Mikel Arteta will feel a little differently about this situation when he sees a replay of what actually happened. https://t.co/tflU7nc831

The Arsenal winger reacted to a heavy challenge, and the referee has judged that he kicked out. There was very little in the incident, a slight movement of his left leg rather than a full-on swing.

RED CARD for Max Dowman! 🟥 https://t.co/wq4EvRIScm

Fleetwood’s best attacking moment of the second half! White and Mosquera got themselves in a mess before Meslier made a smothering save from Davies. Havertz heads the resulting corner clear but Eze messes up a promising Arsenal break.

Arsenal continue to hog possession around the Fleetwood box, but since both teams made their subs, the home team have started to look more comfortable again. Eze’s shot is blocked, and then he is caught offside.

Arsenal making another couple of changes: Guimaraes and Konsa replace Lewis-Skelly and Zubimendi.

For Fleetwood: Davies replaces Loupalo-Bi.

Ben White caught offside just as Arsenal were building up a head of steam in attack. “Champion of England, you’re having a laugh” is the chant from the home fans.

From that Arsenal free-kick, Havertz’s low cross goes straight into the side-netting. The German has had a bit of a stinker, Arsenal will need better at Anfield on Sunday. I’m sure Arteta would have liked to have taken off Havertz or Gyokeres by now.

Haughey wins an important tackle on Lewis-Skelly after Arsenal found the free player in the box, and from the resulting short corner Dowman’s shot is straight Lynch.

Dowman is then hacked down by Batty, who was tempted in by a heavy touch. Booking for the Fleetwood defender.

If the game finishes level, we will go straight to penalties. One or two players on both teams with heavy legs, but Arsenal surely have to turn the screw from here.

Coughlan is an in-form striker who is trying to offer Fleetwood some more intensity and pressing from the front. Despite all that Arsenal pressure, Fleetwood have not gone under since conceding the equaliser.

Havertz hesitant after Odegaard picked out his run and split the Fleetwood defence again. Neither let fly with the shot from a tight angle, nor picked out a cutback. Two changes from Fleetwood: Evans and McClean off, Coughlan and Murphy on.

And a change from Arsenal: O’Neill off, replaced by Eze. O’Neill was one of Arsenal’s brighter starters.

Bodies on the line from Fleetwood to keep the scores level, first Havertz and then Lewis Skelly had shots blocked from a free-kick floated into the box. Fleetwood need to hope for a second wind from somewhere.

Odegaard with another delightful flicked pass, but Havertz could only poke the ball into the side netting. Should be doing better with that chance, he had half of the goal to aim at. Arsenal knocking on the door, feels like a second goal is coming.

Havertz’s rebound actually flicked off Bennett’s head, or else that was a certain goal. As you would expect, Fleetwood now finding it very difficult to get out of their half or establish any possession. The combination of Odegaard’s introduction, the tactical tweak and some choice words look to have done the trick.

Superb double save from the Fleetwood goalkeeper Lynch, beating away Dowman’s shot and then getting a hand to Havertz’s volley on the follow up. It was a switch of play from Odegaard to start the move, and an immaculate first touch from Dowman.

O’Neill has shown some quick feet and no shortage of skill down the left for Arsenal early in the second half, McLean is booked for a trip. Odegaard close to splitting the Fleetwood defence with a reverse pass. One-way traffic now.

They will not be hanging this one in the National Gallery, but Arsenal are level. Bright play from O’Neill down the left, putting his marker on his heels and whipping early delivery into the box. Gyokeres needed a couple of stabs at it, but the application of studs on ball was enough to sneak it beyond the goalkeeper.

Martin Odegaard has done more in five minutes than any of the 11 who were on the pitch in the first half. A class act, the best midfielder in the Premier League when he is on song.

Viktor Gyökeres gets his first goal of the season and Arsenal are level against Fleetwood! 🔴 https://t.co/LfZcIbAfCX

Arsenal camped in the Fleetwood half, but yet to carve out that clear-cut chance. When they have the ball, Hincapie, Mosquera and White are playing as a back three. Odegaard enjoying plenty of touches early in the half.

Can Arsenal shift up a gear or two in the second half? White for Timber feels pre-planned but Arteta will not have wanted to call for Odegaard at this stage.

No messing around here from Arsenal. Martin Odegaard and Ben White have both done a rigorous half-time warm up and will be introduced immediately.

Odegaard and White on, replacing Timber and Salmon. I think that means Lewis-Skelly to left-back.

Arsenal waste a corner just before half-time whistle, and they have 45 minutes to spare themselves an embarrassing League Cup exit to League Two Fleetwood Town. The home team scored with their only shot of the game, with Arsenal’s defence undone a little too easily and Marli Salmon exposed.

Since then, Arsenal have dominated possession but have not produced enough quality around the box. Still a long way to go, but a mammoth cup shock at least feels possible.

Half a chance for Jurrien Timber, but he misdirects his glancing header from Dowman’s free-kick. Dowman’s set-piece delivery has been excellent in difficult conditions.

Fleetwood enjoy a spell of territory in the Arsenal half,  Loupalo-Bi leading the line well again before Lewis-Skelly’s backpass put Meslier under some pressure.

Meslier claimed the resulting long throw well, and bowled out a quick throw to Gyokeres, but Batty sprinted back to ease out the Arsenal striker a little too easily.

There will be seven minutes of added time to play. The pattern of the game is fixed now, but Arsenal are not creating enough danger from their heaps of possession.

Hincapie whips a cross through the Fleetwood penalty area, but no Arsenal player was on the end of it in the six-yard box. We await to find out how much stoppage time there is to play.

More menace about Arsenal’s last few attacks, with Lewis-Skelly and Havertz combining and then Bennett doing ever so well to clear Dowman’s driven cross. Havertz then skews a header wide, from another Dowman delivery.

Lots of Arsenal possession without really stretching the Fleetwood defence, before Ched Evans buys a foul against Mosquera to relieve the pressure. Arteta will want the players on the pitch to figure things out, without him having to call for some big guns off the bench.

Hincapie and Mosquera have not played much Premier League football, and it is showing in their passing so far. Quality of Arsenal’s build-up from the back has been scratchy, making it easier for Fleetwood to set themselves behind the ball.

Gyokeres with a snap shot that he was always stretching for and it was simple work for the goalkeeper Lynch. Half hour gone, but we will be playing until almost 55 minutes in this first half.

Hincapie’s pass towards O’Neill goes astray. Fleetwood’s defensive shape is serving them well so far, they are defending in a 5-4-1 are limiting space. When Arsenal do lose the ball, they look open. They needed a Zubimendi interception to thwart a counter-attack after a Mosquera givaway.

Max Dowman runs out of room down the right as some rain swirls around the stadium. I’m not sure there will be any panic in the Arsenal ranks, but they need to be crisper than they have been so far.

Something of a scramble from a wide Arsenal free-kick but the home team survive and there is a huge roar from the home crowd. Lewis-Skelly then slips in midfield and Loupalo-Bi helps drag Fleetwood up the pitch.

One of the two Fleetwood players to come into the team from the defeat by Exeter has scored, Loupalo-Bi. He pinned Salmon as the last man and rolled the young Arsenal defender, before poking the ball through the legs of Meslier. Loupalo-Bi is on loan from Fulham. Is the shock of all shocks on?

Well, well, well. The stadium reeks of sulphur from the red plumes of smoke that have been set off in celebration. Whatever criticisms you have of English football, a night like this when the minnows serve it up to giants is exactly what makes the sport great. Fleetwood might not hold on but, goodness, they have given the locals something to enjoy.

First big chance of the game falls to Arsenal. Salmon’s pass forward deflected through to Dowman, but he scuffed the ball across goal with his right foot just in front of Gyokeres. Could he have run around the ball and curled the shot with his left? He looked to have had the time.

Arsenal starting to apply some pressure now, and the attacks are coming from their right flank through Timber and Dowman. Rooney wins a crunching 50:50 at the edge of the box to deny Lewis-Skelly a clear shot on goal. Great block.

Another throw-in for Fleetwood high up the pitch, won by Ched Evans. Fleetwood need all of the levellers they can get tonight, and you wonder if that long stoppage right from the off can be one.

The throw-in is dangerous again, but Hincapie defends well at the back post.

Fleetwood enjoying their first passages of possession, and they win a throw-in deep in the Arsenal half, Hincapie putting the ball out.

Batty is going to launch this into the box... it’s a flat and powerful long ball but Lewis-Skelly cleared after the ball was flicked on. Havertz then wins a free-kick.

According the Peter Drury in the Sky Sports commentary box, police have now located the operator of the drone and believe the situation is under control.

We go back to the free-kick Arsenal won eight-and-a-half minutes ago.

Dowman’s delivery was excellent, but Hincapie failed to win clean contact on the header.

Play is yet to resume. The referee is currently talking to Matt Lawlor and Mikel Arteta on the touchline.

Not ideal for either team when it comes to injury prevention, aside from everything else. A shame for Fleetwood and the spectacle.

Just when you think you have seen everything in football, we now have play stopped because of a drone and the players are being brought off. There is plenty of anger in the stands about this, too. We had 57 seconds of play and now we are into the eighth minute of the game being halted. Absolutely absurd.

Arsenal get the game under way at a pretty blustery Highbury, but the pitch looks in lush condition.

Red fireworks and Together in Electric Dreams greet the teams.

The Highbury Chippy has been doing a roaring trade and plenty of customers from north London enjoyed the chance to wallow in some nostalgia. One man who isn’t interested in sentiment is Mikel Arteta and the strength of the team he has named indicates how serious he is about going all the way in this competition. Max Dowman is going to be in everyone’s gaze but this is an important night for Viktor Gyokeres, who has a chance to build up his confidence after a disappointing start to the campaign.

The Arsenal midfielder suffered a broken nose just a few minutes after coming on as a substitute against Everton.

We made two changes, one enforced through suspension. We had to make changes because we have a packed schedule and we have the champions coming to town and there’s a way we want to go and play.

The steepest from winning the league last year. It will be a very difficult challenge we have to come up against. They have paid a lot of respect to the competition and us by naming such a strong team. We understand it’s a difficult challenge.

It’s always very special, this competition and coming to these kinds of grounds, it’s proper English football. We’re very excited about it and we’re going to take it seriously.

It’s great to have Marli, Max and Ceadach with us, and Illan as well, who since he’s joined, hasn’t had the opportunity to start a game. We always say everybody’s going to be important, they need to feel like it, and the only way to do that is to play minutes.

For sure, because that’s the best way to express yourself, when you have the chance and you have to play. Give me a headache, give me a problem, and give me reasons to play more. So far, the boys have done that very well.

A curious quirk of their modern history is that Arsenal have won eight of their last nine FA Cup finals – Liverpool in 2001 their one defeat – but have lost four League Cup finals in a row since they last won the competition in 1993.

Arsène Wenger used the competition to blood younger players, and that remains the case for Arsenal despite them carrying a bigger, more experienced squad nowadays.

Nevertheless, given the impressive record of Jurgen Klopp’s Liverpool and Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City in the League Cup, it is an itch Arteta will want to scratch.

Arteta’s Arsenal have not won a major final in front of fans, and they are too good a side to allow that state of affairs to drag on.

Did he pick up a knock against Everton or has he been rested? I suspect it could be the former, because he was a candidate to start and give either Havertz or Odeegaard the night off.

Aaron Loupalo-Bi comes into the team from the weekend’s defeat at Exeter City. Ched Evans is their centre-forward.

Fleetwood Town XI: Lynch, Rooney, Haughey, Potter, Neal, Bennett, McLean, Helm, Batty, Evans, Loupalo-Bi

Subs: Pradic, Andrew, Cannon, Davies, Thomas, Murphy, Coughlan, Robertson, Cirino

Starting against the Arsenal. 🖇️ 🤝 Fox Group https://t.co/1dHunJopWv

They are the three youngsters in Mikel Arteta’s team. It’s a debut for Ceadach O’Neill. Timber, Lewis-Skelly and Havertz are the three starters who could start at Anfield, so I would not expect 90 minutes from any of them. Raya, Gabriel, Calafiori and Rice the first-teamers given the night off. So too Noni Madueke, which speaks to his rising status within the squad.

Arsenal XI: Meslier; Timber, Salmon, Mosquera, Hincapie; Zubimendi, Lewis-Skelly; Dowman, Havertz, O’Neill; Gyokeres

Subs: Kepa, White, Odegaard, Guimaraes, Eze, Konsa, Harriman-Annous, Washington, Hashi

🔵 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🟡 Your Carabao Cup Gunners 👊 🤝 @deel

Bruno Guimaraes, Martin Odegaard, Kai Havertz and Eberechi Eze are among the players stepping off the bus, so at the very least it will be a strong bench.

Aside from their stadium being called Highbury, Fleetwood Town’s red shirts with white sleeves also bear a striking resemblance to Arsenal’s home kit. The club in its current guise was founded in 1997, although previous iterations date back to 1908 under the name Fleetwood FC.

There is no evidence or anecdote suggesting Arsenal were the inspiration, so it appears the kit clash is a coincidence. Arsenal will be wearing their navy away strip.

The club’s most famous son is surely Jamie Vardy, who scored 31 goals in 36 appearances for Fleetwood in the 2011-12 season before Leicester City made their move.

An unfamiliar opponent at a very familiar sounding venue, Arsenal play Fleetwood Town for the first time this evening at the Lancashire club’s Highbury Stadium.

Fleetwood, 18th in League Two, are the lowest-ranked team remaining in this season’s League Cup, having booked their place in the fourth round thanks to a victory at Sheffield United.

They were playing in English football’s sixth tier in 2009, and so while their stadium may share its name with Arsenal’s former home, the two clubs are worlds apart.

The League Cup is fourth of four competitions on Arsenal’s list of priorities, but Mikel Arteta should be able to rotate extensively while progressing to the quarter-finals. With a trip to Anfield on Sunday, that is a welcome luxury.

Kepa Arrizabalaga, Piero Hincapie, Cristhian Mosquera, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino and Viktor Gyokeres are seasoned internationals in need of minutes and in line to start.

Max Dowman lit up Arsenal’s third-round victory at Ipswich Town, and 17-year-old centre-back Marli Salmon was not far behind him. Young striker and Northern Ireland international Ceadach O’Neill is also expected to be involved, and he may be joined by other academy players.

While attention is fixed on Premier League and Champions League success, Arsenal’s stinging defeat by Manchester City in last season’s final of this competition will not have been forgotten by Arteta or his players.

Matt Lawlor, Fleetwood’s manager, was full of praise for Arsenal in his pre-match press conference: “The champions are coming to town and they’re coming to our patch. The players need to be excited by it, not overawed by it. The respect is through the roof, but the fear can’t be through the roof.

“We’ve earned a game like this. We’ve had to go through round upon round of tough games, and none of them were easy. To get to where we are, we deserve that.”

Arteta has told his players that they must keep their standards high, with a lack of concentration or professionalism potentially their worst enemy against fourth-tier opposition.

Arteta said: “Our reputation, our pride, everything is in play. So every time you play a football match, and especially against a team in a different division, respect the game, respect every opponent because they deserve that, and then try to win and try to play a bit better than them.“We know the risk, and in football, things can get very equal the moment you are able to match certain things, and that’s why our basics and habits have to be through the roof to be able to win the game.”Full team news on the way shortly.

#1213. Guardiola explains to Romario why he should be patient with Ancelotti

Pep Guardiola defended Carlo Ancelotti during an interview with Brazil legend Romario, explaining to his former Barcelona teammate why he should be patient with the Italian tactician: ‘How many World Cups has Brazil played?’

Romario has been one of Ancelotti’s harshest critics, especially after the Seleçao’s elimination from the 2026 World Cup Round of 16.

Guardiola has faced Ancelotti’s teams many times and clearly doesn’t share his former Barcelona teammate’s view.

“How many World Cups has Brazil played? Million! You’ve lost more than you’ve won,” Guardiola said.

Romario argued that he’s not annoyed that Brazil don’t win, but by the way they play.

“I’ve coached Brazilian players, and everyone says the pressure here is greater than anywhere else. It’s very hard,” Guardiola replied.

“I know Carlo a bit. I’ve played against him many times; he’s beaten me a million times. He’s an extraordinary person, and I have no doubt about his ability. He’s come to a new country, to a new culture, and sometimes you need a bit more time. You know there isn’t enough time to train a national team. We’ll see what happens.

“[It happens to] most of the coaches who go from a club to a national team for the first time. I believe that, in the end, football is football; you have less time and have to adapt, but I’m sorry, Mario, I couldn’t doubt Carlo’s ability; it’s impossible, impossible. I know him. People say, ‘He’s good at managing the group’; everyone says he’s the best. I faced him, and he’s very smart. He makes tactical decisions. He knows, as I do, that if you don’t win, you won’t last. Why did I stay at Manchester City for so many years? Because we won a lot. If not, you go home.”

Romario and Guardiola also spoke about their defeat in the 1994 Champions League Final against Fabio Capello’s Milan.

Romario asked Pep whether that Milan side were technically stronger than their Barcelona, but Pep seemed unsure.

“They were very strong, very, very strong. We were too, but they were really strong,” he said.

“It’s very hard with Italian football. Capello had his way of playing, different from Johan’s [Cruijff], but they were a top side.”

In the same interview, Guardiola spoke for the first time about rejecting an offer to coach Italy’s national team last summer, saying he needed to rest and admitting he could have accepted the proposal if it had come at a different time in his life.

Lorenzo Bettoni is the Editor of Football Italia.

#1212. Welcome to the Man United madhouse, Mauricio! Man United emerge from the chaos at Sporting Lisbon with a draw as Senne Lammens joins their band of self-saboteurs in game that had it all, writes CHRIS WHEELER

Published: 17:18 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 19:22 EST, 25 November 2026

A week into the job and Mauricio Pochettino must be getting used to the madness of Manchester United by now.

If it's not drones flying over the training ground, red card controversies and random divots of grass, it's his own players shooting themselves in the foot.

At least, Pochettino emerged from the craziness in Lisbon with a draw on a night when Bruno Fernandes celebrated his return to the Jose Alvalade Stadium with a couple of goals.

But these are the kind of nights that must drive coaches like Pochettino potty. After the carnage of Michael Carrick's final two games in charge against Roma and Aston Villa, and the rancour of the Argentine's introduction to the Old Trafford circus at Anfield on Sunday, this was another mad, mad spectacle.

Where do we start? The two acts of self-sabotage by goalkeeper Senne Lammens? United's two disallowed goals? The first was harsh on the scorer, Amad Diallo, but also Youri Tielemans who received a booking that led to his sending-off in injury-time. Or maybe that divot, which Fernandes claimed he created and then hit to put United ahead with a bizarre deflected goal?

At the end of all the chaos, United had conceded five penalties in their last five games and picked up four red cards.

Senne Lammens (left) two errors cost Man United a deserving win at Sporting as they drew

New United head coach Mauricio Pochettino comforts Lammens at full-time after his mistakes

That is not something that will sit well with Pochettino. But after venting his frustration with the officiating over Leny Yoro's sending-off at Anfield, which dominated the build-up to this game after it was rescinded, here was another sequence of events that seemed to conspire against him.

It's not as if the Jose Alvalade Stadium was a cauldron of emotion to scramble the senses of the two sets of players and match officials either. Fernandes got a polite round of applause from the fans and a framed memento from his old club before kick-off.

When the teams came out, he was one of three former United players alongside Cristiano Ronaldo and Luis Nani honoured on a tifo of the Sporting Lisbon greats.

It was all very flat until the half-hour mark when United self-imploded again. Geny Catamo picked up the ball on the edge of the United box and teased Lisandro Martinez, playing at left back.

Martinez took the bait and stuck his leg out. He barely caught Sporting's No 10 and it took Catamo a full second to realise he had, before going down theatrically and earning a very soft penalty from Polish referee Szymon Marciniak.

Sporting's top scorer Luis Suarez stepped up and made it easy for Lammens to make the save. It was a let-off for United and potentially a big moment in a difficult season for Lammens.

But he undid his good work 75 seconds later when Maxi Araujo chased a long ball over the top pursued by Noussair Mazraoui. For some reason, Lammens thought it would be a good idea to race 25 yards out of his goal.

Araujo stepped inside the Belgium goalkeeper and went down under his clumsy challenge. Marciniak pointed to the spot again, and this time Suarez made no mistake.

Lammens started positively saving this Luis Suarez penalty before conceding a spot-kick

Yet, minutes later Suarez scored after being given a second penalty following Lammens error

United thought they had eqaulised before half-time but Amad Diallo's header was ruled out for a percieved foul in the build-up by Youri Tielemans that earned him a booking

After all the upset over the officiating at Anfield, United were on the wrong end of another big call just before half-time here when Tielemans stretched to poke the ball through to Diallo and inadvertently caught Goncalo Inacio who went down claiming serious injury.

Goalkeeper Kaique Pereira saved Diallo's first effort and Marciniak blew his whistle for a foul before the Ivorian headed in at the second attempt so there was no opportunity for VAR to review it. The referee booked Tielemans, but there was a strong argument that it wasn't even a foul.

United re-emerged for the second half undeterred and hit back to score twice through Fernandes within five minutes of the restart.

The United captain played the ball through for Martinez and then converted from the spot after his team-mate went down in a tangle of legs with Eduardo Quaresma.

Bruno Fernandes levelled for United just after half-time when they were awarded a penalty

He then put them ahead with this left-footed shot that hit a divot on the pitch before flying in

United's lead was undone late on when Lammens' second major error allowed Suarez to score

United's evening was compounded when Tielemans was sent off late on for a second yellow

Two minutes later, and having made the divot turning in the penalty box 17 seconds earlier, Fernandes somehow managed to hit it with a hopeful effort from 25 yards. Pereira had the ball covered but it took an outrageous deflection just outside the six-yard box and flew through his arms.

But this is United and nothing is straightforward. In the 80th minute, with victory within their grasp, Lammens had all the time in the world to catch a high ball from Ivan Fresneda. Perhaps too long. Unforgivably, he dropped it in front of Suarez who hooked into the net.

There was still time for more drama when United had another goal from a Fernandes' corner chalked off for Patrick Dorgu's foul on Pereira, after VAR sent Marciniak to the monitor, and he then showed Tielemans a second yellow card.

Pochettino looked on frustrated and probably as confused as the rest of us.

Manchester United are facing growing uncertainty over Bruno Fernandes’ future after Juventus joined AC Milan in expressing interest in signing the Portuguese midfielder next summer.

The 32-year-old has temporarily put contract negotiations on hold, preferring to concentrate on helping United recover from their disappointing start to the Premier League season under new manager Mauricio Pochettino.

However, the lack of progress over a new agreement has encouraged some of Europe’s biggest clubs to explore the possibility of signing him.

According to Italian publication Tuttosport, Juventus are monitoring Fernandes’ contract situation with a view to potentially signing him without a transfer fee next summer.

AC Milan are also interested, with manager Ruben Amorim keen on reuniting with his former Manchester United captain. The pair share the same representative agency, potentially giving Milan an advantage in future negotiations.

Fernandes is already familiar with Italian football, having previously represented Novara, Udinese and Sampdoria before returning to Portugal.

A recent CaughtOffside report revealed that Fernandes has reportedly rejected United’s last two contract proposals, leaving negotiations at a standstill.

However, Man United retain the option to extend his existing agreement until 2028, meaning a free transfer next summer is far from guaranteed.

Losing Fernandes would represent an enormous setback for United, particularly during such an important rebuilding period.

Despite being 32, the Portuguese international remains one of the team’s most influential players, offering creativity, leadership and goals from midfield.

United should understandably consider his age when discussing a long-term extension, but allowing a player of his quality to leave without receiving a transfer fee would make little financial or sporting sense.

The responsibility now falls on Pochettino and the club’s hierarchy to demonstrate that United are moving in the right direction.

Fernandes has previously turned down opportunities to leave Old Trafford, but his loyalty should not be taken for granted.

Juventus and Milan could offer an attractive alternative if United’s struggles continue.

Activating his contract extension would provide temporary security, but convincing Fernandes that he can still compete for major honours in Manchester should remain the ultimate priority.

#1209. Neto: ‘Excited’ to play for Juventus again after almost ten years

Brazilian goalkeeper Neto will start for Juventus in a Europa League game against Omonia FC tomorrow: ‘I’m really excited to be back on the pitch.’

The experienced goalkeeper returned to Turin on a free transfer in September, replacing the injured Kamil Grabara.

The Poland international suffered a season-ending knee injury, urging Juventus to sign a replacement.

Neto has not played a competitive match since May 30 with Botafogo, and last played for Juventus nearly ten years ago, in May 2017, helping them beat Lazio 2-0 in a Coppa Italia Final.

“It’s hugely satisfying. I’m really excited to be back on the pitch, and proud to be part of this team,” Neto said at a press conference today, as quoted by Ilbianconero.com.

“Football and life go through different cycles, and there are different people involved. I see a very healthy environment for achieving our goals, and that’s what we need to maintain: the belief that we’re on the right track.

“I was at a point where I was looking for certain things, and whatever I did in the next stage of my life had to make sense,” he added when asked about his return to Juventus.

“I was looking for something that would inspire me. When this opportunity came along, I felt that. It had a different meaning. Deep down, I felt my chapter with Juve was still open.

“I’m very happy and satisfied. I enjoy my work, and whatever comes in the future is in God’s hands. I’m here to help, and whatever happens will happen.

“We’re in a place where, wherever you look, you see so many trophies. Whether we talk about it or not, there’s no need to spell it out: we know where we are and what we represent. I’m here to try to achieve great results, and I sense the same ambition around me. Hopefully we can get there. Just like the other teams, we want to win. That’s what we’re fighting for.”

Juventus sit fifth in the Europa League standings with ten points in four matches, but have had very different results in Serie A, where they have already lost three games from 12 and sit 6th in the table, six points behind Milan in four.

Neto, however, has plenty of confidence in his teammates.

“Seeing and feeling the desire these lads have, with so many young players willing to contribute, is truly infectious. From my perspective, that’s a positive thing,” the 37-year-old said.

“There are important players here. We’re talking about Juve. We have the team, the desire and the determination, and hopefully we can get there.

“Every competition is difficult these days. We are Juventus, and whenever Juventus play, we have a responsibility to compete to win. That’s our goal. I haven’t looked at what lies ahead, because at this club you have to fight to win. That’s how it is for me, and I imagine it’s the same for everyone.

“This is a developing team with lots of young players who may be playing in this league for the first time and are still finding their feet. There can be ups and downs. The season is so long that we can’t focus solely on this moment, because in a month we might be talking about something else. My focus is always on giving 100% in training. We need to find balance and consistency.”

Omonia FC have grabbed two wins and two defeats in four Europa League games so far and sit 18th in the table.

“It will be a difficult match. They’re a very strong team,” insisted Neto.

“We’ve watched them, and they counterattack with real quality. I know Fabiano from our time in Brazil. Every game in Europe is difficult, and we know the challenges involved.”

Juventus’ first-choice goalkeeper Vicario will rest tomorrow. He’s on loan from Tottenham, but does he deserve to remain at Juventus long-term?

“I don’t know how much my opinion matters, but he’s a top-level goalkeeper,” Neto concluded.

Lorenzo Bettoni is the Editor of Football Italia.

Tottenham Hotspur are stepping up their interest in Benfica striker Vangelis Pavlidis as Roberto De Zerbi assesses potential attacking reinforcements ahead of the January transfer window.

The 28-year-old Greece international has established himself as one of the most prolific goalscorers in European football, attracting considerable attention from Premier League clubs following his outstanding start to the season.

Tottenham are now closely monitoring his performances, although convincing Benfica to sanction a mid-season departure could prove difficult.

According to Portuguese publication Record, Tottenham have regularly sent scouts to Benfica matches specifically to assess Pavlidis.

The Greek forward has scored an impressive 19 goals in 20 appearances across all competitions this season, further enhancing his reputation as a reliable goalscorer.

Pavlidis has become an important figure in Benfica’s attack, contributing through his movement, physical presence and ability to involve teammates in attacking moves.

However, Tottenham are not alone in their admiration for the striker.

A recent CaughtOffside report revealed that Manchester United are also interested in securing his services.

Benfica’s negotiating position remains strong, with Pavlidis understood to have a €100million release clause in his contract. There is currently no indication that Tottenham have submitted a formal offer.

Signing Pavlidis would represent an interesting departure from Tottenham’s emphasis on recruiting younger players with significant resale potential.

At 28, the Greek international is already in his prime and would arrive with considerable experience rather than requiring several seasons of development.

His intelligent movement inside the penalty area, finishing ability and willingness to contribute outside the box could make him particularly effective in De Zerbi’s attacking system.

However, Tottenham must be careful about the financial commitment involved.

While Pavlidis has consistently delivered goals in Portugal and previously in the Netherlands, adapting to the intensity of Premier League football would present a fresh challenge.

Spending close to his release clause would represent a substantial gamble, particularly given his age.

If Tottenham can negotiate a considerably lower transfer fee, Pavlidis could prove an excellent addition capable of making an immediate impact.

For now, continuing to assess the striker before committing to an expensive January pursuit appears to be the sensible approach.

Arsenal have added Club Brugge winger Carlos Forbs to their list of January transfer targets as Mikel Arteta looks to inject more pace and creativity into his attack.

The 22-year-old Portugal international has rebuilt his reputation in Belgium following difficult spells with Ajax and Wolverhampton Wanderers, attracting renewed interest from several Premier League clubs.

However, Arsenal may have to wait until next summer to secure his signature, with Club Brugge reluctant to lose one of their most influential attacking players.

According to Football Insider, Forbs features prominently on Arsenal’s shortlist of left-sided attacking targets ahead of the January transfer window.

However, Club Brugge have already informed the Gunners that the Portuguese winger is not available for a mid-season transfer, particularly with the Belgian club still competing in the Champions League.

Forbs has registered five goals and seven assists across all competitions this season, having contributed to 22 goals during the previous campaign.

The former Manchester City academy player has also impressed at international level, recently scoring Portugal’s winning goal against Wales in the Nations League.

A recent CaughtOffside report revealed that Club Brugge could demand around €30million for Forbs, who remains under contract until 2029. Manchester United and Tottenham have also been monitoring his progress.

Arsenal’s interest in Forbs is understandable, particularly given his explosive acceleration and ability to take on defenders.

Arteta’s side regularly encounter opponents who defend in compact formations, and having another winger capable of beating players individually could help create opportunities in difficult matches.

His versatility across both flanks would also provide valuable rotation and reduce Arsenal’s dependence on Bukayo Saka.

However, his disappointing loan spell at Wolves cannot be completely overlooked. Performing consistently in Belgium and succeeding in the Premier League are two very different challenges.

At around €30million, Forbs could nevertheless represent an attractive alternative to some of Arsenal’s considerably more expensive attacking targets.

The Gunners should avoid paying an inflated January premium simply to overcome Club Brugge’s reluctance to sell.

Continuing to monitor his development before revisiting negotiations next summer would be a sensible approach, particularly if Forbs maintains his impressive performances in European and international football.

Manchester City could face a major battle to retain Erling Haaland next summer, with the Norwegian striker reportedly considering a move away from the Etihad Stadium amid growing uncertainty surrounding the club.

The 26-year-old remains one of the most prolific goalscorers in world football, but City’s disappointing performances and the possibility of significant financial sanctions have fuelled speculation about his long-term future.

Barcelona are emerging as a particularly attractive destination should Haaland decide to pursue a new challenge in 2027.

According to Spanish publication El Nacional, Haaland is seriously considering his future at Manchester City, with Barcelona among his preferred destinations.

City’s recent 2-2 Champions League draw against Napoli highlighted their ongoing struggles, with the English giants managing just one victory in their last five matches across all competitions.

The uncertainty surrounding potential sanctions for City’s financial breaches has further complicated the situation.

Barcelona have long admired Haaland, and the prospect of pairing the Norwegian with Lamine Yamal would undoubtedly appeal to the Catalan giants.

An earlier CaughtOffside report also revealed that Barcelona were monitoring Haaland’s situation following developments in City’s financial case.

However, the striker remains contracted to Man City until 2034 and has not publicly submitted a transfer request.

Losing Haaland would represent an enormous setback for City, both on the pitch and commercially.

Replacing a striker of his quality would be exceptionally difficult, particularly if financial restrictions or potential sporting sanctions limit City’s recruitment capabilities.

From Barcelona’s perspective, signing Haaland would be a statement of intent. His exceptional finishing ability and movement could complement Yamal’s creativity and establish a formidable attacking partnership.

However, Barcelona’s financial limitations remain a significant obstacle. Even if Haaland expresses a desire to leave, convincing City to accept an affordable transfer fee would be another challenge entirely.

City’s immediate priority should be restoring consistency on the pitch and demonstrating that they can continue competing for major honours.

Haaland is entering the prime years of his career, and retaining him will require more than contractual security.

City must give their most valuable player convincing reasons to believe his ambitions can still be fulfilled at the Etihad Stadium.

Manchester United remain open to selling Marcus Rashford in January despite bringing the England international back into the first-team squad following his loan spell at Barcelona.

The 29-year-old returned to Old Trafford during the summer after the Spanish giants decided against signing him permanently. Although United publicly backed his reintegration, uncertainty continues to surround his long-term future.

With Mauricio Pochettino looking to reshape his squad during the winter transfer window, Rashford could once again find himself facing an uncertain future in Manchester.

Speaking on the Market Madness podcast, transfer journalist Ben Jacobs revealed that United would still entertain suitable offers for Rashford despite their public stance regarding his return.

United are also struggling for attacking consistency, making the departure of an experienced forward potentially counterproductive unless a suitable replacement is secured.

At 29, Rashford still has enough time to rediscover his best form, although he must demonstrate greater consistency and availability.

Pochettino’s arrival offers the academy graduate another opportunity to revive his United career.

If Rashford fails to impress under the new manager, a summer departure could make sense. For now, though, United should prioritise getting him fit and assessing his contribution before making a definitive decision.

#1200. Wesley Fofana’s Chelsea nightmare continues as Liverpool win shoot-out

Unfortunately for Chelsea, Wesley Fofana put his hand up twice. Firstly to concede the first-half penalty for handball that allowed Liverpool to equalise quickly after Chelsea themselves had scored from the spot.

And secondly to volunteer to take one of the penalties in the shoot-out. The defender had to score to keep Chelsea in it, but he woefully, nervously skied his effort high into a gleeful Kop and it was Liverpool who went through to the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup.

LIVERPOOL ARE THROUGH TO THE QUARTER-FINALS OF THE CARABAO CUP! 🔴 Wesley Fofana blazes over to hand Liverpool their FIFTH consecutive victory ✅ https://t.co/M4n01R8DSk

There the reward for Andoni Iraola, the head coach, is a home tie against the club he left in the summer: Bournemouth. The draw has opened up for Liverpool, and they know it, with only Manchester City left of the other big guns. But despite again playing at Anfield, they would have preferred not to face such a dangerous and motivated opponent, who have just reeled off five wins and five clean sheets in a row under Iraola’s replacement, Marco Rose.

This was also a big win. A meaningful win. One that was celebrated as such with Dua Lipa’s One Kiss – an anthem on Jürgen Klopp’s run to Liverpool’s first Champions League final under him in 2018 – played over the loudspeakers at the end as the players joyfully milled around the pitch.

One kiss is all it takes 🎶 https://t.co/0jfujy4V94

“I am happy to feel it. We feel the support,” Iraola said when asked whether he sensed the momentum and togetherness building in his reshaped Liverpool side. It looks as though they are.

Fofana was Chelsea’s eighth taker, so they were running out of options, but it was a truly terrible effort. The 25-year-old turned and scratched his head – just as many Chelsea fans have done over his underwhelming, albeit injury-hit, contributions since his eyebrow-raising £75m move from Leicester City in 2022.

Both sides had the chance to win it earlier in the shoot-out. For Liverpool it was Kostas Tsimikas, who had taken the decisive kick to beat Chelsea in a shoot-out in the 2022 FA Cup final, but the Greek full-back also completely missed the target.

Tsimikas has the chance to put Liverpool through... And fires over the bar! 😱 https://t.co/eCKBT6njMB

Then Chelsea striker Emmanuel Emegha – on his debut – saw his kick saved, after an effort by Ryan Gravenberch had also been stopped. In the end, Liverpool’s stand-in captain Joe Gomez – still to score an actual goal – crashed in his kick before Fofana’s blunder. The 29-year-old Gomez finally “scored” and it was an assured strike.

This was the fifth penalty shoot-out between these two clubs, in all competitions, with Liverpool having now triumphed in all five. They won the toss for this one and elected to take the kicks in front of the Kop, which roared its satisfaction and did its best to unsettle the Chelsea takers.

Both stand-in goalkeepers – Giorgi Mamardashvili and Mike Penders – made one outstanding save each in the shoot-out. Chelsea substitute Valentín Barco was the other player to miss, hitting a post.

Chelsea blink first in the shootout! 🔵 Valentín Barco's penalty bounces off the post... https://t.co/rSXGfQctbI

The other efforts, in truth, were outstanding and assured with Liverpool, undoubtedly, benefitting from Iraola turning to his bench and bringing on Alexander Isak, Alexis Mac Allister, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola. All scored their penalties.

Among Chelsea’s scorers was Jordan Henderson and the former Liverpool captain received a strange homecoming in his first appearance at Anfield for three years. He was booed, in the first half at least, and especially when he tucked the ball under his arm before Chelsea took their penalty – in normal time – which gave them the lead. Henderson turned to the stands, grinning.

Morgan Rogers buries the spotkick! ⚽️ Chelsea take the lead at Anfield 🔵 https://t.co/YlDn2gakRi

In truth it was more pantomime than meaningful and Henderson, like another former, Champions League-winning Liverpool midfielder Xabi Alonso – now Chelsea’s head coach – did not celebrate as Morgan Rogers scored. The penalty came after a rash challenge by Gravenberch, who crashed into Moisés Caicedo as the Chelsea captain ran on to Malo Gusto’s shrewd reverse pass inside the area.

Afterwards, Alonso faced more questions about his decision not to use Estêvão Willian. Despite injury to João Pedro and Cole Palmer’s suspension, there was only a place on the Chelsea bench for the 19-year-old Brazilian. And he stayed there even though Alonso used all five substitutions. More than two years have passed since Rio Ngumoha chose to leave Chelsea for Liverpool, but the frustration remains at Stamford Bridge. The pain of losing a player of Ngumoha’s potential does not pass quickly, especially as the winger was part of Chelsea’s academy system for eight years. It must sting to see a London boy, one of their own, now delighting the Anfield crowd.

For many at Chelsea, the anger at Ngumoha’s departure in 2024 will probably never subside. Or, at least, it will not subside while he continues to develop so thrillingly at Liverpool. Such was Chelsea’s annoyance at the time of his exit, Telegraph Sport reported last year, Liverpool’s scouts were subsequently banned from attending matches at their academy centre.

It is an all-Premier League tie at Anfield as Liverpool host Chelsea in the last 16 of the League Cup, with a place in the quarter-finals at stake. This will be the first managerial meeting between childhood friends Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso.

Liverpool beat Tottenham 3-1 at Anfield in the last round of this competition, which included a stunning goal from Dominik Szoboszlai to seal progression to the last 16. They earned their first home Premier League win of the season on the weekend as they beat Brighton 2-0. Iraola’s men come into this game off the back of four straight wins in all competitions.

“There will definitely be changes, but we want to win the game and we want to be competitive,” Iraola said ahead of this tie. “We have to see how the legs; we are not just in the Carabao Cup, but also in the Champions League and we have been trying to make changes from game to game. We want to be in the next round. We have been unlucky in the draw, playing Chelsea, and they have been unlucky also. But we want to be in the draw again and that only happens if you win. We need to rotate, all the top teams need to rotate when you are playing every three days. Sometimes you are forced to rotate due to injury or sometimes different demands in different games tactically. I am happy that everyone is involved. When we have had to use someone who has not played a lot of games, they have helped us. The more players we have in a good place, the easier my selection will be, even if it is hard to leave players out.”

Giovanni Leoni, Conor Bradley and Hugo Ekitike remain long-term absentees for the hosts with Jeremie Frimpong also missing. Florian Wirtz could feature despite going off with an ankle knock during the win over Brighton.

Like Liverpool, Chelsea also had an all-Premier League tie in the third round of this competition, beating Leeds 6-3 in a high-scoring affair at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea come into tonight’s game off the back of a 2-0 defeat against Tottenham in the league last weekend. Not only did they lose on Saturday but to make matters worse for them Cole Palmer was sent off. As a result of that red card, Palmer is suspended for tonight’s tie.

“We [Alonso and Palmer] spoke and for sure he knows the mistake he made,” Alonso said. “Things that you can avoid. I hope that this is not going to be repeated. He is aware of that, he is mature and it was a mistake. He is in a good space, he connects very well socially with his teammates. They like him, they want Cole smiling, they want Cole having fun, enjoying his game because when we see that, he will have a better team. I will just ask you because he has got this very cool persona, you probably know his personality is very interesting.”

Former Liverpool midfielder and current Chelsea boss Alonso has lost his two games as a manager against Liverpool; a 4-0 defeat as Bayer Leverkusen boss and then a 1-0 loss when in charge of Real Madrid, with both taking place at Anfield. Alonso is not the only ex-Liverpool midfielder to return to Anfield tonight as their former captain Jordan Henderson is in the Chelsea squad for tonight. Joao Pedro has missed the trip to Anfield because of a thigh injury which could rule him out for a few weeks.

The Premier league fixture between these sides at Anfield ended in a 1-1 draw back in May. In that match, Arne Slot was in charge of Liverpool with Calum McFarlane in interim charge of Chelsea. Chelsea won the reverse fixture 2-1 at Stamford Bridge. Team news from Anfield to follow shortly.

#1199. Montella: ‘Turkiye ambition, Milan chaos, Roma success and my apology to Capello’

Former Turkiye manager Vincenzo Montella looks back over his career, including the ‘chaos’ at Milan and ‘never believing’ in Cristiano Ronaldo, plus why he ‘must apologise’ to Fabio Capello.

The Little Aeroplane is now a free agent after he was dismissed by the Turkiye squad for losing all their Nations League games, despite taking them into the Nations League A and qualifying for the 2026 World Cup.

“When I arrived, they were afraid that they wouldn’t qualify for the European Championships, but we did it, and then got into the World Cup and the Nations League A,” Montella told La Gazzetta dello Sport.

“Naturally, the end to this experience hurt, but at times unpredictable things can happen in football.”

His playing career was most closely associated with Roma, and it is also where he made his senior debut as a coach.

“Making my debut on the Roma bench at the age of 36 was special. I already enjoyed reading the game from the touchline, especially when I started to spend a lot of time on the bench as a player, but when you become a coach, it opens up a whole new world.”

Montella’s first major job was at Silvio Berlscuoni’s Milan in 2016, but there were more downs than ups.

“It was always my dream, because I supported Milan when I was a kid, seeing Marco van Basten. Berlusconi was a gentleman, even if he often got involved and tried to push me towards certain decisions. He was accustomed to a squad full of Ballon d’Or winners, but we didn’t have them. I joked that if he bought me one, I could play more attacking football too.

“That club had more publicity slogans than concrete messages. There was a lot of chaos in the second year, a change of ownership, many new players, and just a general chaos in the transfer strategy. We didn’t always share ideas, sometimes I wasn’t even consulted.

“I think when the time came to sign a striker, I was told the budget was all used up.”

There had been talk that summer about Cristiano Ronaldo coming to Milan, before his experience at Juventus.

“I never believed in that, it seemed more like Fantasy Football,” insisted Montella.

When it comes to another of his former clubs, he has high hopes for Gian Piero Gasperini’s Roma, especially with Donyell Malen scoring four goals in a single game.

“I scored four in the derby, though, marked by Alessandro Nesta, so it’s a bit different,” smiled the former striker about his record in 2002.

“I do think Malen will be the Capocannoniere this season, if he keeps going like this, he can get 30 or more. Roma can challenge for the Scudetto to the end, then who knows?”

Roma have not won the Scudetto since 2001, when Capello was the coach and Montella the striker along with Francesco Totti and Gabriel Batistuta.

“We had a big party at my house the day after the final game. Capello was not invited, but he turned up anyway. If I had opened the door, I’d have made him run around the building a couple of times first,” revealed Montella.

“I do think I owe Capello an apology, at times I didn’t behave professionally, and I regret that.”

Manchester United reportedly look set to miss out on the potential signing of Leeds United striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin as he’s closing in on a new contract at Elland Road.

The England international has been in superb form for Leeds, scoring 14 Premier League goals for them last season and starting brightly with five in his first eleven games so far this term.

As recently reported via the Daily Briefing, our understanding is that this led to Man Utd enquiring about Calvert-Lewin as they look for signings up front this January.

However, the Red Devils have had to move on to other targets such as Ivan Toney as it already looked clear at that stage that Calvert-Lewin was looking likely to stay and sign a new deal with Leeds.

Ben Jacobs has now reported the update below on Calvert-Lewin, in what looks like a huge boost for Leeds…

Calvert-Lewin x Leeds renewal, as revealed yesterday.? https://t.co/X5NOARSx3Q

— Ben Jacobs (@JacobsBen) November 25, 2026

LUFC boss Daniel Farke will surely be delighted by this news, as will the club’s fans, as the 29-year-old clearly has the quality to be one of the Premier League’s top strikers on his day.

Calvert-Lewin had been a star player for Everton not that long ago, but it’s fair to say his time there ended on a bit of a low, and he’s made the most of this new challenge and change of scene.

Want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

This is just the kind of player Leeds are going to need if they are to establish themselves as a Premier League club again after a bit of yo-yoing between the top flight and the Championship in recent years.

It’s also easy to see why United looked at Calvert-Lewin as he could have added the quality and experience they’re lacking right now as they look in genuine danger of a relegation battle this season.
