#1187. Amorim: ‘Milan must do well in Europa League and Serie A, only way to be a good team’

Ruben Amorim warns Olympiacos are ‘aggressive, especially at home’ in the Europa League, but Milan ‘have to do well both in the League and in Europe, it’s the only way to be a good team.’

It kicks off in Athens on Thursday at 17.45 GMT (18.45 CET).

Injuries are piling up for this trip, with Luka Modric, Strahinja Pavlovic, Francesco Camarda and Davide Bartesaghi joining Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Fikayo Tomori, Matteo Gabbia, Samuel Chukwueze, Alexis Saelemaekers and Pietro Terracciano on the treatment table.

At least Mike Maignan is available again after suspension, and confidence was boosted by a 5-1 Serie A victory over Frosinone.

“It’s a fact that we need to improve in the final third,” said Amorim in his press conference.

“The only thing we can do is improve our principles. We need to improve on these little things, and that’s the only way I can help my players. Against Olympiacos, it will be a different match than the one against Frosinone, just as it will be different than the one against Cagliari.

“We need to improve, even in our defending. We’ve almost always conceded a goal, so that’s another area we need to improve.”

Olympiacos are sixth in the Europa League table after amassing 10 points from four games, beating Jagiellonia, Olympique Marseille and Sparta Prague before the 0-0 draw away to Stade Rennais.

Notably, they have conceded only one goal in those four matches.

“They’re a strong team. They’re aggressive, especially at home. I’ve played here twice, and it was tough for me. I know their coach and what he wants to do. They play compact, positive football, 4-3-3, they change a lot, they rotate, they have Jota, a lot of Portuguese players.

“They’re a strong team, and with their fans there, it’ll be a tough match. Chiquinho is a great talent, but very impulsive. I hope he plays well tomorrow, but I hope he still has a great career ahead of him.”

The Rossoneri’s form in the Europa League has been little short of disastrous, as the 4-0 victory away to RB Salzburg was an outlier between three defeats to Benfica, Bournemouth and Ferencvaros, all without scoring a single goal.

“To be a good team, you have to do well both in the league and in Europe,” insisted Amorim.

“That’s the only way to be a good team. We have to be, especially at Milan. I’m always waiting for things to go badly, because it doesn’t take much to change the situation. That’s what I’m trying to make my players understand, because it won’t always be this way. We’re at the beginning of a process, and I think we need everyone.

“We lost Pavlovic, Modric, Saelemaekers, Chukwueze, and everyone has to be ready, because there are no excuses at big clubs. We have to be ready for this. I can’t believe we lost all these games in Europe because we rotated.

“We have to always be ready and approach the games like against Inter, Frosinone, and Genoa. We’re building so many things. Tomorrow is another test for us.”

Does Amorim still believe that Milan will be able to challenge for the Scudetto?

“I haven’t changed my mind. This year is difficult, but if we have the chance to fight, we’ll do it.”

Many coaches have been asked about the release of the Grand Theft Auto VI game and how much time players are committing to it.

“I’d rather my players play that every day rather than scroll through social media,” replied Amorim.

“Social media, and all that stuff, is very difficult for players, who in any case live with more criticism than I do. After Frosinone, I haven’t read anything, because that’s how I want to live my life.”

#1186. Ben Jacobs: Tottenham Could Sign Ivan Toney On One Condition

Tottenham could make a move to sign Ivan Toney during the January transfer window, on one condition, according to GIVEMESPORT sources.

Signing a new centre-forward could be one of Spurs' priorities in the upcoming window.

Although Tottenham brought in Omar Marmoush from Manchester City in the summer, they have lost Brazilian forward Richarlison as an option.

The former Everton man was close to a departure in the summer but remained at Tottenham. Roberto De Zerbi then opted to not name him in his Premier League squad, meaning he hasn't been involved with the first team this season.

As a result, he's likely to depart in January, so we could see Tottenham look to sign a replacement.

Dominic Solanke has also been incredibly inconsistent since his move to Spurs, so signing a prolific forward could be a smart move.

Speaking on the GIVEMESPORT Market Madness podcast, senior correspondent Ben Jacobs has confirmed that Tottenham could be interested in signing Toney in January.

It will depend on whether a loan is possible for the England international and, of course, if he's keen on leaving the club.

"I would imagine if Toney says that suddenly he's not happy in Saudi Arabia, and it's an increasingly volatile, political situation there, if a loan becomes available, clubs like Man Utd or even Spurs may be prepared to entertain that one. It's kind of too early to tell. One, because we have to see whether the Saudi Pro League continues to be affected by politics, and two, because Toney has always said, certainly when Matthias Jaissle was at Al-Ahli, that he was happy in Saudi. If that changes in the winter market, then a move to the Premier League could be of interest."

Signing a player of Toney's calibre on loan would certainly be a smart move for Tottenham.

Of course, the wages would be a concern, but if they can secure his signature in a deal that makes sense financially, he'd certainly benefit De Zerbi's squad.

Well, they're playing in Saudi. Toney is still banging in the goals, with 15 in 15 games so far this season.

Spurs are ready to sanction their first January transfer window deal

If Toney, described as 'one of the best strikers in the world by Al-Ahil sporting director Rui Pedro, does become available on loan in the January transfer window, you'd imagine a host of different clubs will show interest in securing his signature.

He could be the perfect addition for many sides, especially in the middle of the season when you just need some extra firepower up top.

Manchester United, for example, could certainly do with another striker, while he might look to reunite with Thomas Frank at Crystal Palace.

Tottenham would likely have to offer him guaranteed minutes, and it will be interesting to see who De Zerbi thinks is his first choice if Toney does arrive.

#1185. Man Utd Fans Slam ‘Embarrassing’ Player After 2-2 Sporting CP Draw

In their second game since Mauricio Pochettino took over from Michael Carrick, Manchester United took on Sporting CP. The Red Devils had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

Having been thumped 4-0 by Liverpool in his first match in charge, the Argentine would have been desperate for a fast start in the Champions League. The first half, however, did not go to plan as the Red Devils conceded two penalties.

After Lisandro Martinez gave away the first, Senne Lammens made a save from 12 yards but then conceded another penalty only minutes later. This time, Sporting star Luis Suarez made no mistake, as he scored the second of his two spot kicks.

After the break, Martinez won the third penalty of the game, this time for the Red Devils when he was tripped in the box. Bruno Fernandes tucked home the first goal of the Pochettino era and then gave Man Utd a lead just two minutes later. His tame shot from the edge of the box took a strange deflection off a divot in the ground, and somehow found the back of the net.

United looked in control, but with 10 minutes to go, Lammens made a complete mess of claiming a cross, fumbling the ball. Suarez reacted brilliantly to acrobatically make it 2-2. Pochettino's men thought they'd taken a lead shortly after, but VAR intervened to rule out a goal after Kaique Pereira was deemed to have been fouled when trying to claim a corner.

There was then time for Youri Tielemans to get himself sent off late on for a second bookable offence, as the game ended 2-2. Man Utd fans will have to wait a little longer before seeing their first win under Pochettino.

While there was plenty of anger aimed at Lammens after the goalkeeper's errors, another player has also been blamed for the disappointing draw.

Despite Lammens having a horror display, giving away a penalty and then being at fault for the second goal as well, many Man Utd fans online instead turned their fury on Noussair Mazraoui. Starting ahead of the much-maligned Diogo Dalot, the Moroccan didn't fare any better.

Mazraoui lasted just 64 minutes before being replaced by the Portugal international. Unimpressed with his efforts, supporters on social media tore into the right-back, with one remarking:

"If Mazraoui starts next season with us, then I'll have no choice but to consider the Manchester United board shameless. Man has been dropping stinkers in almost every game."

Another added: "Dalot is worse than Mazraoui but Mazraoui is also worse than Dalot." While a third wrote: "Dalot in 5 mins has shown why he is far better than Mazraoui."

Someone added: "Mazraoui is trash guys we gave to accept it." Another summed up the mood, writing: "Mazraoui was not good enough for Bayern, what made the board think he’d be good enough for United?"

One more added: "Just keeps getting worse every week, Martinez & Mazraoui are embarrassing."

#1184. Chivu: ‘Inter must be best version of ourselves’ against VfB Stuttgart

Cristian Chivu wants Inter to be ‘the best version of ourselves’ in the Champions League against VfB Stuttgart this evening, with an update on Lautaro Martinez.

It kicks off at San Siro at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game and PSG-Roma on the Champions League Liveblog.

The Nerazzurri’s confidence took a knock on Sunday in Serie A when they fumbled a 4-2 lead for the chaotic 4-4 draw away to Atalanta.

They are also playing catch-up in Europe, having lost the first two matches against Real Madrid and Club Brugge, then got back on track beating Shakhtar Donetsk and Feyenoord.

“We must be the best version of ourselves,” Chivu told Sky Sport Italia.

“We are well aware of the importance of this match, we are playing at home, and must give a sense of consistency to our recent good performances in the Champions League.”

VfB Stuttgart are one point ahead of Inter in the Champions League table going into tonight’s match, as they won the first two, drew 1-1 with Atletico Madrid, and lost 2-0 away to Galatasaray.

Pio Esposito scored a hat-trick against Atalanta at the weekend and Lautaro Martinez made his comeback after more than a month out, but is not risked from the start tonight.

“Lautaro is recovering his fitness and ready to come on in the second half. Marcus Thuram has played practically non-stop in recent months, and we need him again this evening,” explained Chivu.

#1183. Spurs win three in row for first time in 616 days to pile pressure on Sage

For the first time in 616 days, Tottenham Hotspur have won three Premier League matches in a row. Three different managers have been sacked in that time, and the mood in north London had plunged to grim lows, but finally there is a sense that something truly exciting is stirring at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

This victory over Crystal Palace was not as impressive as last week’s triumph at Chelsea, but it did not need to be. After Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off in the 13th minute, Spurs simply had to make their numerical advantage count. They did so with relative ease, taking complete control of possession and creating endless goalscoring opportunities.

Roberto De Zerbi’s team ended the night with 34 shots to Palace’s two and with 758 completed passes to Palace’s 149. The goals ultimately came from two defenders, Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke, but there was a long list of Spurs players who might have scored here.

Spurs take the lead through an Archie Gray header! ⚪ https://t.co/qSCECkOJur

Did this defeat mark the end for Pierre Sage, the Palace manager? The Frenchman was only appointed in June but it has been a grisly start to the campaign. Palace have the worst defence in the league, have lost six of nine games and have not produced any truly encouraging performances in the Premier League.

Even in the two games Palace have won, against Fulham and Nottingham Forest, they were lucky to do so. The likes of Sean Dyche and Thomas Frank, both of whom would be strong candidates to replace Sage if Palace do pull the trigger, will no doubt have been keeping an eye on events here.

“I am really aware of the situation,” Sage said. “I don’t like this situation. [But] you can trust in me, I will never give up. I want to be the first on the pitch on Monday. I have the rage to train more. It’s not me to decide this thing [his future]. If I have one hour, I will give my best for one hour. If I have 10 years, I will give my best for 10 years.”

The decision for Palace chairman Steve Parish, then, is whether this result represented a continuation of the team’s problems or was an aberration caused by the early red card. It would be reasonable for Sage to claim this match was out of his hands from the moment Mateta lunged at Spurs captain Micky van de Ven, but such an argument might not carry much weight with Palace sitting 18th in the table.

The challenge was foolish in the extreme by Mateta, a player who was much more successful in exiting this game than he has been in his numerous attempts to leave Palace in recent transfer windows. At first glance it did not seem the worst tackle, but the replays were damning: Mateta led with his studs and made forceful contact with Van de Ven’s ankle.

It was an inexcusably brainless act, after just 13 minutes of play, and the same could be said of Palace’s defending from a right-wing corner a few minutes later. Mohammed Kudus swirled the delivery to the back post, where Gray was unmarked. Yes, Palace were defending with 10. But no, that does not justify the inability of Sage’s players to spot Gray. Even more embarrassingly, the Tottenham player was unmarked again from another corner shortly afterwards.

It was not the first time this season that Palace’s cause has been undermined by a red card. When they lost at home to Ipswich Town in September, Axel Disasi was sent off after 34 minutes. An absence of discipline? Perhaps. Sage might argue, though, that he is not responsible for his players demonstrating a lack of basic brainpower.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League encounter between Tottenham and Crystal Palace.

Last weekend, Spurs enjoyed a historic result, beating Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the league for 36 years thanks to Mike Penders’ own goal and Mathys Tel’s stunning solo strike. This result, coupled with the 3-1 victory over Coventry City in their previous home outing, means that Tottenham have won back-to-back league games and are beginning to gather some momentum under Roberto De Zerbi.

In his pre-match press conference, when asked if he’s felt a change in atmosphere after the triumph at Stamford Bridge, De Zerbi replied: “We have not achieved our goal. We want our fans to be happy, not now, at the end of the season. Now we have to push, we have to stay focused, we have to increase the spirit, the appetite to win games in a row. To do that, we have to show if we are good enough. If we are good enough on the pitch, for sure we are ready. In the head, in the mentality, we have to show, because the step of this club is to win games in a row and to be angry day by day, game by game, win by win. One time or two times are not enough.”

Palace have endured a tricky and inconsistent start to the season under their summer appointment Pierre Sage, accumulating just seven points from their opening seven league matches while shipping 17 goals. The 1-0 League Cup victory over Fulham in midweek has momentarily eased the pressure on the Frenchman, but given their newfound success in recent campaigns, fan expectations have risen, with recent performances prompting some cause for concern.

Tottenham remain without the suspended Rodrigo Bentancur, while Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall, Savio, Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhaylo Mudryk are out injured. James Maddison was substituted early in the second half at Chelsea with an apparent groin strain, but De Zerbi insists he’s available for this one. Destiny Udogie could also be involved after recovering from a knee issue.

The visitors are without the injured trio of Ismaila Sarr, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chadi Riad, but there’s hope that Quinten Timber and Jorgen Strand Larsen are fit to be involved this evening after they both missed the Fulham victory.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with teams coming shortly.

#1182. The untold story of Mauricio Pochettino's move to Man United: When club decided he was the right man, the moment it became 'real', emotional talks with US staff and whirlwind first days in charge

Published: 21:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 04:25 EST, 22 November 2026

When Mauricio Pochettino boarded a flight from London to Atlanta a little over two weeks ago, there was little indication that by the time he landed back in the UK it would be as the new head coach of Manchester United.

The club were aware of the £7.5million buyout clause in his contract with the US national team as they began to consider potential replacements for Michael Carrick, but it hadn’t gone any further than that.

However, United’s 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on October 25 left Carrick’s job hanging by a thread. He was given a two-week stay of execution that also allowed United time to step up their search for a suitable replacement.

At a meeting of the club’s executive committee on November 5 – after United had lost to Chelsea and staged a chaotic Champions League win against Roma – it was decided that Pochettino would be the No.1 choice if Carrick was sacked.

By the time the Argentine caught that flight to Atlanta 24 hours later to take charge of the USA's two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final against Haiti, United were preparing to make their move.

This is the story of the whirlwind two weeks that will end with Pochettino taking charge of his first game as United boss against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday following the dramatic events on both sides of the Atlantic.

Patrick Dorgu’s injury-time header rescued United from another defeat as they snatched a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford, but it wasn’t enough to save Carrick. His fate was effectively sealed and the first contact was made with Pochettino’s camp.

There is a five-hour time difference between Manchester and Georgia, so it was late afternoon when Pochettino first learned of United’s interest at the Trilith Guesthouse – close to the US national team’s training base in Fayetteville south-west of Atlanta – as the players began to report there for duty.

Michael Carrick's fate was effectively sealed and the first contact was made with Pochettino’s camp after the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford

As speculation raged over Carrick’s future, the odds on Pochettino replacing him at Old Trafford were slashed after some big money was placed on the 54-year-old overnight.

Preliminary talks continued with his representatives who made the US Soccer Federation aware of the situation. Pochettino discussed it over dinner at the team hotel with chief executive JT Batson and chief operating officer Dan Helfrich who knew it was pointless trying to change his mind.

‘That was the big day,’ says a source close to Pochettino, who took US team training in Fayetteville. ‘It became real and the optimism grew.’

As talks accelerated between United and their prospective new head coach, Carrick returned to Carrington to work with the United players not on international duty while chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew to Monaco to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and rubber-stamp the change.

United reached verbal agreement with Pochettino over a two-and-a-half-year deal, and agreed to pay US Soccer around £10million to buy the 54-year-old and his staff – No 2 Jesus Perez, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino (Mauricio’s son), strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott – out of their contracts.

There was never any question of him leaving before the two Haiti ties, even though it left little time before his first game against Liverpool. Pochettino is said to have been respectful of the USA’s position and felt an obligation to see the job through.

As a compromise, it was agreed that Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr would be allowed to leave for Manchester after the first leg regardless of the result.

Media in the US were informed that access to the players had been cancelled out of respect for Veterans Day. It also meant that they don’t have to answer questions about Pochettino’s future.

Carrick returned to Carrington at 7.50am for the last time as United head coach and was sacked in a meeting with Berrada and Wilcox.

By the time Pochettino woke up in Fayetteville, United officially had a managerial vacancy and he gathered the players together for a scheduled team briefing at 10am.

Pochettino went through the usual pre-match preparation, and then invited staff into the room for the second half of the meeting.

There was some emotion but no surprise when he informed them of his decision to take the United job. ‘As you’d expect, he spoke from the heart,’ says a source. ‘He loved being here but United was a dream opportunity. It was too hard to say no, but hard to say goodbye.’

United officially announced Pochettino’s appointment and confirmed that he would stay in charge for the USA’s two games against Haiti before starting work the following Wednesday.

Pochettino conducted his pre-match press conference in Fayetteville, flanked by CEO chief JT Batson and president Cindy Parlow Cone, and broke down in tears as he thanked them for their support over the last 26 months.

Otherwise, the preparation is said to have gone according to plan as the US squad flew to Miami.

The Argentine broke down in tears as he thanked the USA for their support over the last 26 months

The US smashed Haiti 6-0 to all but guarantee their place in the semi-finals. Even so the message from Pochettino to his players after the game was: ‘This tie isn’t over.’

The players learned for the first time that Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr were leaving camp, and they headed straight to Manchester.

Pochettino flew with the players from Miami to Cincinnati for the second leg at the TQL Stadium.

On a visit to the Kenwood Towne Centre shopping mall, a man whose profile had risen in the US during his two years in charge of the national team was approached by even more fans than normal.

When Pochettino appeared as a guest of honour at the NFL game between the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium that night, a number of Bengals’ players and staff congratulated him on his new job claiming to be United fans.

It emerged that United had provided a private jet for Pochettino and the remainder of his staff to fly straight from Cincinnati to Manchester through the night after the second leg.

In his pre-match press conference, he confirmed the departure of his three coaches over the weekend, and it was no surprise to learn that he was in constant contact over several days as he prepared to join them at Carrington.

The US beat Haiti by two goals to complete an 8-0 aggregate win. Afterwards, they played Take Me Home, Country Roads by John Denver over the stadium PA, which has been a tradition since the US hosted the World Cup last summer but carried particular poignance given that it has also been adopted as an anthem at United.

Pochettino invited all the staff onto the pitch for a team photo as he led a chant of U-S-A, and there was a tearful send-off in the dressing-room as he was presented with a signed shirt and a special hand-painted bottle of Clase Azul tequila.

It’s a favourite tipple of Pochettino’s and staff also ordered food from Chick-fil-A, which Pochettino regrets won’t be available in Manchester.

He never had a permanent residence in America, so he left the stadium at 10.30pm with the same suitcase he had brought from London and headed for Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport for the flight to Manchester.

Pochettino had a poor night’s sleep before landing shortly before noon aboard the grey Gulfstream G700 jet with D’Agostino, Scott and Tuya.

He posted a picture from the skies above Manchester and was then driven to Carrington, changing into an official United tracksuit en route.

Pochettino was too late for training but met with some of the players and club executives before being given a tour of the training ground and conducting an interview with MUTV which wrapped up about 7pm. He stayed at the training ground long into the evening to catch up on his preparation for Liverpool.

The plane believed to be carrying Pochettino and his staff was hired by Manchester United

More players returned from international duty, but Pochettino’s first training session with them at Carrington was ambushed by a drone shooting video footage that was posted online. It was proof – if he needed it – that the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss will be under even greater scrutiny at United.

Responding, Pochettino said: 'We have young guys training with us. It’s not nice. It’s not good.

'What do they want to show? Yes, we were working on shape. We were very organised. What is the point of doing something that can be very dangerous?

'I don't want to be upset, but I think it's a process the club is caring a lot about.'

Pochettino’s first training session with them at Carrington was ambushed by a drone shooting video footage that was posted online

Having only trained for a couple of hours on Thursday, Pochettino worked with the players between 11.30am and 2pm on Friday.

‘The training session was a little bit longer than it normally is in (match day) minus two,’ said Pochettino at his opening pre-match press conference, admitting that he had not even had a chance to shower beforehand.

Pochettino worked with his new players between 11.30am and 2pm on Friday

Pochettino took training for the third day running at Carrington on Saturday morning, before United travelled on the team bus to their hotel where they had dinner and a pre-match meeting last night.

On Sunday he faces a massive first game as United boss in front of the cameras at Anfield at the end of a dizzying fortnight.

#1181. Arsenal Thought They Signed a 'Phenom' in Miyaichi, but things went wrong

Back in 2011, Arsenal had built up a reputation for identifying some of the most talented players, whether it was Nicolas Anelka, Aaron Ramsey or Theo Walcott. The Gunners did some wise business, and they thought they had done the same with Ryo Miyaichi when they plucked from obscurity in 2011, offering him a trial.

Arséne Wenger was impressed by Miyachi when he had a trial with the club, and he offered the Japanese youngster a professional contract at the end of January of 2011.

The Frenchman said at the time: "We’re delighted that Ryō Miyaichi has joined us. He trialed with us in the summer and has raw ability which has attracted many clubs around the world". Some believed at the time that he could be the 'next Lionel Messi'.

"Ryo has natural technical ability. He has good balance and phenomenal pace, and his passing and crossing is consistently of a high quality. He is a very exciting player." - Wenger on Miyaichi in 2011

Miyaichi was an ultra-skillful player who quickly impressed in the youth ranks, both for club and country, and he was on course to become a star. In fact, during his first senior spell in professional football, on loan at Feyenoord, he was nicknamed 'Ryodinho' by the Dutch media, which only sparked excitement among Arsenal fans.

"I like his pace, his mobility and his movement off the ball. I like players who can move when others have the ball. There is also his attitude, commitment and desire. That is why I decided to keep him." - Wenger on Miyaichi in 2011

He went on to spend time at Bolton Wanderers and then Wigan Athletic, where he suffered a long-term ankle injury that saw him miss their successful FA Cup campaign.

By this point, Miyaichi had managed just one senior league appearance for Arsenal, and after a loan spell with Twente back in the Netherlands, he was released by the Gunners. Miyaichi later reflected: "Back then, I didn't really think of myself as young. There were so many world-class players around my age, and I was always feeling pressed."

The Japan international found a new permanent home at St Pauli, but his debut was significantly delayed by an ACL rupture, and after returning to action, he ruptured the ACL in his other leg in a horrible run of luck.

Remarkably, the German side still renewed the winger's contract. Sporting chief Andreas Rettig explained: “Ryo has unbelievable bad luck, and we do not want to leave him alone. [We want to] show that we are behind him. We hope that this decision will help Ryo to return to his old level of performance.”

Reflecting on his career at a later date, Miyaichi went on to say: "At one point, I seriously thought about quitting soccer.

"I have been away from the team for long periods and have caused trouble time and again. I have also disappointed many people. That is why I thought about quitting."

He went on to enjoy a couple of seasons of full fitness before being released in 2021 after racking up 77 league appearances. It was at that stage that he returned to Japan, joining Yokohoma F. Marinos, where he has been since, racking up 104 league appearances and scoring eight times. Back in 2022, he actually added three more Japan caps to his name, which must have been nice for him after all the injury troubles that followed his first two caps in 2012.

At 33 years of age, Miyaichi is still playing with Yokohoma F. Marinos, and he won the JLeague with them back in 2022, adding to the two FA Cups he technically won between Wigan in 2013 and Arsenal in 2014.

Speaking back in June on why he wants to keep playing, Miyaichi said: "I think having fun is the most important thing. It's what fuels your growth. I still have the desire to keep improving and still feel the same way I always did. Showing people something that makes them think is cool on the pitch is what I'm there for."

Miyaichi's never-ending battles with injury must have made for a tough time, but fueled by his love for the game, he never gave up, and perseverance has allowed him to keep playing at the age of 33. Things could have gone a very different way for the winger, even if his biggest hopes were not fulfilled.

Tzolis' 64% pass rate and 16 turnovers underlined a stale forward line, forcing Arteta into a risky selection call.

#1180. Engineering signalling centres to trigger human trunk morphogenesis in vitro

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Vertebrate trunk development is orchestrated by endogenous signalling centres that generate gradients of signals such as WNT and BMP to pattern cell fates and drive morphogenesis1,2,3,4,5,6,7. Whether these cues alone can reconstitute human trunk-like morphogenesis in vitro remains unknown. Here we present a synthetic embryology platform for high-throughput, spatiotemporal delivery of morphogen signals to epithelial cysts derived from human pluripotent stem cells. Transient WNT and BMP gradients are sufficient to drive the generation of axially elongating trunk-like structures that contain a central neural tube flanked by axial, paraxial, intermediate and lateral mesoderm. The geometry of the transient BMP signal exerts lasting control over mediolateral patterning and bilateral symmetry. Patterning and morphogenesis are sustained by neuromesodermal and lateral plate mesoderm progenitors induced by the initial cues, which act as endogenous signalling centres. Together, these findings define a minimal spatial code sufficient to reconstitute trunk-like morphogenesis in a human stem-cell-based model and establish a scalable platform for studying early human development and congenital disorders.

The scRNA-seq and bulk RNA-seq data generated for this study are available from the GEO under accessions GSE306808 and GSE347564, respectively. Other reanalysed datasets are available from the following repositories: mouse gastrulation, ArrayExpress (E-MTAB-6967)55; cynomolgus macaque embryo, GEO (GSE193007)56; RA-gastruloid, GEO (GSE208369)57; axial organoid, GEO (GSE220563)17; axioloid, GEO (GSE199576)18; and segmentoid, GEO (GSE195467)19. The confocal and time-lapse datasets are large multichannel image series that are impractical to deposit in full; the measurement tables from which the quantitative imaging panels are plotted are provided in the code repository (Code availability). Raw imaging data, and any additional information required to reanalyse the data reported in this study, are available from the lead contact, S.R., on request; requests will be answered within 1 month and data shared by secure electronic file transfer without restriction. Source data are provided with this paper.

Custom code for image analysis and for bulk RNA-seq and scRNA-seq analysis—including SMD feature selection, clustering and annotation, and the trunk morph–embryo correspondence analyses—is available under the MIT License at GitHub (https://github.com/stevenzwick/zwick-2026-trunk-morphogenesis) and archived at Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22756590)58. Random seeds and exact parameters (intensity thresholds and gates, background offsets, local-threshold window sizes, Gaussian σ, histogram edges, clustering resolutions and curated gene lists) are provided in the repository.

a, A detailed schematic of the workflow is shown: (i) Matrigel is microcontact printed onto the two-layered PDMS stamp (PDMS-ii) using a flat PDMS stamp (PDMS-i). (ii) A thin PDMS microwell array is peeled from the silicon master and overlaid on a glass coverslip. Taller PDMS sidewalls are plasma-bonded along two edges. (iii) Capillary water flow through the microchannels drives localized Matrigel transfer from stamp PDMS-ii onto the PDMS microwell layer at the contact interface. (iv) Cells are seeded onto the transferred Matrigel pattern, overlaid with a silanized coverslip atop the sidewalls, and cultured further with media and microwell-trapped beads. b, Photographs of the experimental setup corresponding to steps a(i–iii): coating the flat stamp (grey border, fourth column, top); PDMS-ii stamps with different patterns (blue border, first column); PDMS microwell layer with wells at different positions (red border, second column); aligned PDMS-ii stamp and PDMS microwell layer in contact (green border, third column); and the application of weight and water flow for transfer (green border, fourth column, bottom). MG, Matrigel; RT, room temperature.

a–d, Design of two-layer PDMS stamp and microwell substrate: a, upper-layer pattern used to print Matrigel features; b, lower-layer embedded microchannels (white denotes channel features); c, assembled two-layer PDMS stamp with a three-dimensional illustration of the assembled stamp below; d, alignment of stamp features and microwell layer, with 120 µm diameter microwells positioned at defined distances from pattern edges. Scale bars, 1 mm. e, Whole-chip images show humidified microcontact printing (HµCP) of Matrigel mixed with fluorescently conjugated BSA (cyan) onto PDMS microwell chip (brightfield, grey), using a four-square stamp pattern. Air bubbles beneath PDMS microwell layer and above glass coverslip are visible in brightfield images. Images are representative of 6 independent experiments (12 chips) with similar results. Scale bars, 1 mm. f, Whole-chip image shows standard microcontact printing (µCP) of fluorescent BSA onto glass to validate stamp pattern from a. Image is representative of 2 independent experiments (5 chips) with similar results. Scale bar, 1 mm. g, Image shows pluripotent epithelial cysts formed 3 days after seeding on a PDMS microwell chip, using stamp pattern from a. A diversity of cyst arrangements, rather than the optimized hexagonal pattern with a central cyst as in Fig. 1, are used to show the flexibility of the approach. Image is representative of 79 independent experiments (145 chips) with similar results. Scale bar, 1 mm. h, Whole-chip epifluorescence image shows pluripotent cysts (DAPI, grey), well-trapped BMP4-coated beads (pseudocoloured red), and pSMAD1/5/9 immunofluorescence (pSMAD, green) 6 h after bead deposition. Image is representative of 6 independent experiments (13 chips) with similar results. Scale bar, 1 mm. i, Representative higher magnification images of cyst arrays with adjacent BMP beads and pSMAD1/5/9 immunofluorescence 6 h after bead deposition, from three independent experiments. (Top row) Five-cyst arrays with one or two beads, from chip in h. (Bottom left) Seven-cyst array with two beads, from an independent experiment. (Bottom right) Five-cyst array with three beads, from an independent experiment. Scale bars, 100 µm. j, (Left) Plot shows normalized pSMAD1/5/9 intensity (pSMAD/DAPI) versus distance from BMP bead, d, for all cysts from chip in h except cysts at centre of arrays (n = 201 cysts; light grey lines, individual cyst profiles; solid lines, mean; shaded areas, ±1 s.d.). (Right) pSMAD1/5/9 intensity in the bead-proximal epithelium of each cyst is plotted against the distance to the nearest bead, dmin, showing a negative correlation (red line, R2 = 0.624; n = 156 cysts) up to a distance of 635 µm, beyond which the intensity is low and uncorrelated (R2 = 0.061; n = 45 cysts). k, (Left) Normalized pSMAD1/5/9 is plotted against angle relative to bead direction (θ - θb) for cysts within responsive regime (d < 635 µm; n = 156 cysts). (Right) The direction of the pSMAD1/5/9 distribution, quantified by its first moment, is plotted as a function of the angle towards the nearest bead, θb (R2 = 0.17, n = 156 cysts). The correlation between pSMAD1/5/9 direction and bead angle is weaker than in Fig. 1f due to the overlapping influence of multiple BMP beads positioned near most cyst arrays in h.

a, (top) Live YFP and merged Brightfield (BF)–YFP images show hexagonally arranged cysts derived from the BMP4-T2A-Achilles reporter hPSC line 6 h after exposure to BMP4-coated beads (pseudocoloured red), with no detectable YFP signal. Images are from one experiment (36 cyst arrays). (bottom) Live images of the cysts from (top) 24 h after bead exposure show the presence of YFP (arrowhead) in some cells adjacent to beads. Images are from one experiment (2 cyst arrays). b, Plot of BMP4 read counts per million (CPM) from bulk RNA sequencing of pluripotent cysts at 0 h, 7 h, and 24 h after BMP bead exposure (n = 3 biologically independent samples per timepoint). Dots, individual samples; bars, mean; error bars, ±1 s.d. BMP5 expression was not detected in any of the samples. c, (left) Brightfield, DAPI (grey) and definitive endoderm marker SOX17 immunofluorescence (cyan) images show spatially arranged cysts after a 2-day exposure to the main experimental conditions, including BMP bead exposure, WNT-driven symmetry breaking, and Activin/Nodal signalling inhibitor A83-01 (above), or without A83-01 (below). Images are from one experiment per condition (with A83-01: 1 chip, 21 cyst arrays; without A83-01: 2 chips, 47 cyst arrays). (right) Bulk RNA-seq analysis of key endodermal genes in cysts under the same two conditions, with (green, n = 3 biologically independent samples) or without A83-01 (purple, n = 2 biologically independent samples). Dots, individual samples; bars, mean; error bars, ±1 s.d. A83-01 prevents endoderm differentiation in all protocols here (Extended Data Fig. 5b, Fig. 4, Supplementary Data 5). d, (left) Plot of DAPI-normalized SOX2 and TBXT intensity versus distance from central cyst of array (“anterior”). TBXT varies more with distance from anterior than distance from bead (Fig. 2c) due to A–P symmetry breaking from geometric cyst arrangement16,17 (Fig. 1b). Black arrow indicates the regime where both TBXT and SOX2 are high, corresponding to NMP differentiation (n = 210 biologically independent cysts; thin lines, individual cyst profiles; thick line, mean; shaded area, 95% confidence interval). (right) Pixel density plot of normalized SOX2 versus TBXT; percentages, fractions of pixels above and below the cutoffs. 28% of pixels are SOX2+ TBXT+, indicative of NMP-like expression. e, Brightfield, DAPI (grey), and TBXT immunofluorescence (cyan) images of three hexagonal cyst arrays without (left) or with a central cyst (right) on the same chip. In the absence of the central cyst, hexagonal cysts are prone to express TBXT on both their inward- and outward-facing poles (white arrowheads), indicating a lack of clear A-P polarity. With the central cyst present, TBXT expression is restricted to the outward-facing pole. Images are representative of 2 independent experiments (12 cyst arrays) with similar results. f, Brightfield and immunofluorescence images of cysts after 2 days of differentiation show FOXF1+ nascent lateral plate mesoderm (LPM, red) proximal to BMP4-coated beads (pseudocoloured red; red arrows top left, white arrows elsewhere), whereas FOXA2+ anterior mesoderm (magenta) and SOX2+ neural progenitors (yellow) are distant from beads. Cysts are from another chip of the same design (Extended Data Fig. 2a). Images are representative of 3 independent experiments with similar results. g, Pixel-density plots of FOXA2 versus FOXF1 (top) and SOX2 versus FOXF1 (bottom) immunofluorescence in day 2 cysts, indicating mutual exclusivity. Colour, log-scaled pixel density normalized to the 99th percentile of bin density; contours, equally spaced iso-density lines; dashed lines, positivity thresholds; percentages, fraction of pixels in each quadrant. n = 7 biologically independent cysts from 3 independent experiments. h, Images of cysts after 2 days of differentiation show FOXF1+ nascent LPM located proximally to BMP beads, FOXA2+ anterior mesoderm distant from beads, and TBXT+ mesoderm at posterior end of cysts. Images are representative of 5 independent experiments with similar results. i, Per-chip fraction of cysts containing FOXF1:Achilles+ cells, plotted as in Fig. 2e, for each condition: adjacent to a BMP bead (“Bead”), no bead (“No Bead”) and adjacent to a bead following BMPR1A knockdown (“KD”). #1179. Marotta: ‘Inter not the only club who like Varela’ after viewing Monza talent

Inter President Beppe Marotta admits they are keeping track of Monza striker Gustavo Varela, but warns ‘we are not the only ones who like him’ on the transfer market.

The Nerazzurri are in action in the Champions League this evening, hosting VfB Stuttgart at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game and PSG-Roma on the Champions League Liveblog.

President Marotta spoke to Sky Sport Italia before kick-off and was inevitably asked about the reports that Inter had been scouting Varela for Monza.

“Inter are not the only ones who like Varela, as there are many other clubs interested too. It is normal also that, being so close to Monza geographically, our directors should visit the games.

“Varela is a wonderful surprise of the Serie A season.”

The Portugal international was relatively unknown before coming to Monza in the summer, but has found the net 11 times in his first 11 Serie A appearances.

There were also two goals in his only Coppa Italia match, a remarkable tally for the 21-year-old, who also earned his first senior cap for Portugal.

Inter are among many clubs keeping a close eye on Varela, after Arsenal, Napoli, Juventus, Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund.

Meanwhile, Marotta was also asked about the negotiations to extend the contract of Carlos Augusto and other figures in the Inter squad.

“We are dealing with professionals who are fond of these colours. They are all eager to continue their experience with us, and we see everything required to have a positive outcome in negotiations.”

#1178. Suzuki howler costs Aston Villa crucial points

Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki went from being serenaded with a chorus of “world’s No 1” to making a bizarre blunder that denied Unai Emery’s side a third successive Premier League victory.

The Villa manager, however, preferred to focus on a string of important saves from Suzuki rather than the uncharacteristic mistake that allowed Fulham to collect a deserved point.

It all went wrong for the hosts just after the hour mark in a match where Fulham provided more than a few scares before finding the net in unexpected fashion.

Alex Iwobi, who had been denied superbly by a Suzuki save just moments earlier, swung in a corner. It was right on top of the Villa goalkeeper, who tried to keep it out but only succeeded in fumbling it over the line. A frantic attempt to gather the ball was in vain and goal-line technology confirmed the goal stood.

Zion Suzuki drops Alex Iwobi's corner and Fulham are level! 🫨 https://t.co/KwLFMRpKqk

Suzuki appeared to have been put off by the presence of Fulham’s Shea Charles, but Emery refused to single out the player for criticism.

“I prefer to speak about the saves that he made,” the Villa manager said. “This is part of football. I think he played fantastically and he is doing a lot of saves so he can make one mistake. It is part of football. We can be mature about this.

“I still want to see consistency. Over the last five Premier League matches, we are winning three and drawing two. It’s not bad but with our poor start it’s not enough.

“We have to change our mind quickly for Tuesday against Barcelona. We want to test ourselves at this level.”

Villa go to the Nou Camp with a 100 per cent Champions League record to their name this season. But they will need to improve on Saturday evening’s performance to get a result in Spain.

As well as Suzuki’s error, a 14th-minute penalty miss from John McGinn also proved costly.

It was awarded after Leon Goretzka, making his full league debut for Villa, saw his header hit Sander Berge’s raised hand. Nobody appealed at the time but referee Sam Barrott was sent to the touchline monitor by VAR to review the incident and gave the spot-kick.

McGinn’s attempt, however, hit the crossbar and the chance to take an early lead went begging. The Villa captain seemed a strange choice to take the spot-kick as he has only ever scored one career penalty, but Emery defended the choice, saying: “We analysed the penalty takers in the squad and it was McGinn here.”

Penalty MISSED! John McGinn hits the bar 💥 https://t.co/2kBYkYA2BY

Nicolas Jackson was on hand to ease Villa’s nerves before the break, though. the Villa manager had said before the game that the striker’s goalscoring capability meant he was capable of matching the likes of Harry Kane. His assessment was backed up by Jackson scoring the opening goal, after 40 minutes, which summed up the striker in one moment of pure power combined with agility.

Collecting Johan Manzambi’s superbly weighted pass, Jackson forced his way past two defenders before sliding in the goal that put Villa ahead.

Emery’s touchline celebrations said it all as the Senegal forward continues to flourish under the man who knew how to get the best out of him at Villarreal.

Nicolas Jackson scores his fifth league goal in five games! 🔥 https://t.co/W0xmFtW1Gt

Suzuki has also flourished under Emery and he kept Villa in the game with some superb saves.

When Antonee Robinson crossed for Gonzalo Garcia, his step over allowed Oscar Bobb in for what looked like his second goal in successive games. But Suzuki pulled off a stunning fingertip save. That had Villa supporters singing: “Zion Suzuki, the world’s No 1”.

Robinson put in another cross and Suzuki got a touch that was enough to make Garcia put his shot wide. Villa were living dangerously and the Japanese goalkeeper made another outstanding stop to keep out Iwobi’s header. But then it all went wrong for Suzuki when he fumbled Iwobi’s corner.

That allowed Fulham’s recent revival under manager, Alvaro Arbeloa, to continue – they now have seven points from their past three games.

“We spoke at half-time about what we had to do,” Arbeloa said. “If you want to win a game you have to fight and I think we have to believe in our way, we’ve shown we can beat anyone in the way that we play but we have to be aggressive.

“We created so many chances and at the end it’s one point in a difficult stadium. I’m so happy with the second half because of the way we played, this is the team that we want to be.”

"This is the first time I've seen him that little bit confused" Rob Green analyses Zion Suzuki's error that lead to Fulham's equaliser 🔍 https://t.co/B3HCivNpwz

"I don't think he gets the flowers he deserves" 💐 Jamie Redknapp is a fan of Calvin Bassey 🫡 https://t.co/R9uravAzRU

“We started the game well. Fulham are a good side, not easy to win [against] but we came in front. We did well but in the second half we gave them more time on the ball. They have good players and they can make chances. We were unlucky with the goal but we tried to keep fighting. It is important not to lose these games.”

On Zion Suzuki’s mistake for Fulham’s equaliser:

“It is frustrating because we do not want to concede goals but it can happen to everyone. Zion is a great guy, great goalkeeper. He will learn from it. We will support him and go again.”

"We should have got more" Calvin Bassey believes Fulham should have came away with three points against Aston Villa ⤵️ https://t.co/pMTMtc4zjS

The final whistle is blown at Villa Park and both sides take a point from the game. Aston Villa took the lead through Jackson but Suzuki’s blunder gifted Fulham the equalising goal. Fulham were fully deserving of a point this evening despite falling behind.

Aston Villa have a free-kick inside the Fulham half late on as Palacios needlessly brings down Jackson. This will go into the Fulham penalty area. Aston Villa take it short before Buendia clips it in. Barkley attempts an overhead kick and his effort is blocked. There are appeals for handball but even if it did hit Berge’s arm he was right next to Barkley. It does hit the arm but that is never a penalty.

Garnacho has a shot blocked from just inside the Fulham penalty area.

Torres has already wasted one good chance with his head from eight yards out and there is another. That probably should have found the corner of the net.

Late double change for Fulham as Muniz and Larsson enter the fray.

Aston Villa are also making a late alteration as Garnacho replaces McGinn.

Chance for Aston Villa. Cash clips in a delivery from the right and Torres has a good chance from eight yards out but the Spaniard’s header goes wide.

Zion Suzuki had big gloves to fill this summer after the sale of Emiliano Martínez but already appears one of the Premier League signings of the summer.

Aston Villa’s new No 1 epitomises the vibrant energy of Unai Emery’s revamped squad and is a goalkeeper perfectly suited to the modern game.

The Japanese international is Villa’s own version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson, who revolutionised English football with a vast range of passing from his own penalty area.

Of all the daft statements to have come out of Aston Villa – and I am including Doug Ellis’s frequent claims that he invented the bicycle kick – it is hard to think of anything as absurd as suing a pundit for speaking the truth.

Jamie Carragher’s common-sense declaration that Villa manager Unai Emery might consider a move to Manchester United – because it is a bigger club – has apparently inflicted such a deep wound to the self-esteem of Nassef Sawiris, the chairman, that he has initiated a legal complaint.

Sawiris’s short statement, which he published on social media on Friday night, consisted of 37 ill-chosen words. It started by accusing Carragher of “unacceptable insults to the club and its fans”, then concluded with the vainglorious declaration that “Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football”.

Aston Villa manager, Unai Emery, is giving a full Premier League debut to Germany midfielder Leon Goretzka against Fulham this evening.

The 31-year-old joined Villa on a free transfer in the summer, but a knee injury prevented him from making an appearance off the bench until this month’s Champions League tie against Fenerbahce.

Asked what role Goretzka would have with Villa, Emery deadpanned: “The first one is to be available to play.”

Emery had also made a cryptic remark about Nicolas Jackson and Johann Manzambi in his Friday press conference. The suggestion was that they had been merely rested for Wednesday’s Carabao Cup defeat at Bournemouth.

But the Spaniard said: “For different reasons, not only rest.”

Whatever he meant is unclear, but both start for Villa tonight.

Fulham have won their last two league games – against Hull and Coventry.

Manager, Alvaro Arbeloa, has made one change with Sander Berge replacing Hugo Larsson in midfield.

Villa are aiming to win three successive league games for the first time in this calendar year. The omens are good as they’ve beaten Fulham in their last seven league meetings at Villa Park.

Tonight sees a battle between two Spaniards at Villa Park as Aston Villa host Fulham. Both sides are looking to bounce back from disappointing midweeks having been knocked out of the League Cup; Aston Villa lost 3-0 at Bournemouth, while Fulham fell to a 1-0 defeat at home against Crystal Palace.

After a slow start to the season in the league, Aston Villa’s form has picked up, which includes handing Manchester City their first defeat of the season a week ago. After this evening, Aston Villa have games against Barcelona and Manchester United before the international break but Unai Emery has insisted his full focus is on this game.

“If we are thinking after the match against Fulham, then we are making a mistake and we are completely wrong,” Emery said. “We are prioritising the Premier League, and this is the message. To keep our consistency and demands means that each match is a test.”

Having failed to win any of their first six league games, Fulham have now won back-to-back Premier League games, with consecutive 1-0 wins over Hull and Coventry, which has lifted them out of the relegation zone.

“It [managing in England] is a very tough challenge but I am so happy to be here,” Alvaro Arbeloa said. “I am where I want to be and I am really enjoying my days. I want to win games and I think we are performing well but we need to improve.

“They [Aston Villa] are very compact, they defend so well and even with the ball they know what they have to do. And they have top players, and when you have a top coach with top players, normally you have a top team. I think right now he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world. He is very, very good, he improves everything every year. It does not matter where he is coaching, he is doing an amazing job, and for me also it is a very good challenge to face him.”

In the two league meetings between these sides last season, it was one win apiece; Aston Villa won this fixture 3-1 just over a year ago before Fulham won 1-0 at Craven Cottage back in April. Team news from Villa Park to follow shortly.

#1177. US Police Share Statement as English Footballer Shot and Killed in Mississippi

Tragic reports have emerged from the United States, confirming that a young English footballer was shot and killed in Mississippi. The local police have now shared a statement after making an arrest.

Krissh Mahatma was born in London but had moved to the US to pursue his dream of making it as a footballer. The 18-year-old striker was in his freshman year at Copiah-Lincoln Community College in Wesson, around 45 miles south of Jackson, Mississippi, where the incident took place.

Before moving to the US, he had played for Watford 'A' in the post-16 Community and Education Football Alliance league. Co-Lin announced his signing in February.

As reported by the Daily Mail, Mahatma was fatally struck by a bullet after a gun was fired outside the Green Ghost Tacos restaurant in Jackson at around 3:39 a.m. on Sunday morning.

The English footballer was with his Co-Lin Wolves teammates when they reportedly came across a drunk man outside the restaurant. After a fight broke out, a man pulled out a gun and fired into the group, hitting Mahatma.

The 18-year-old was taken to a nearby hospital via a private vehicle. According to Hinds County Coroner Jeramiah Howard, this was where he died.

Capitol Police have since arrested and charged Danny Luna, 22, with murder. The Mississippi Department of Public Safety did not elaborate on what caused the deadly confrontation. However, in a brief statement, Police Chief Mark Miller sent 'thoughts and prayers' to Mahatma's 'family and loved ones,' adding:

"While this arrest is an important step toward justice, we recognise that nothing can ease the pain of losing a loved one."

Is the Premier League really the best in the world?

Mahatma had made 14 appearances in his first three months with the Co-Lin Wolves, scoring one goal in September in a 3-2 win over National Park College. Co-Lin president Dewayne Middleton issued his own statement on behalf of the college:

"Copiah-Lincoln Community College is mourning the loss of freshman soccer player Krissh Mahatma. Krissh will be deeply missed by his teammates and the entire Co-Lin family."

A fundraiser has been set up to support Mahatma's family and has already raised $31,851 (£24,275). It explained how the young striker was "just beginning a new chapter of life far away from home," before adding: "His sudden passing has left his family, friends, teammates, coaches, and the entire Co-Lin soccer community heartbroken.

"Behind this tragedy is a family grieving the loss of their son and loved ones trying to make sense of a loss that feels impossible to put into words."

The owner of the Green Ghost Tacos eatery, nearby where the shooting took place, said: "On behalf of the entire Green Ghost family, I extend my deepest and most heartfelt condolences to the family, friends, loved ones, and university community mourning the tragic loss of a young student. Our hearts are heavy, and our thoughts and prayers are with everyone affected by this devastating incident.

"While this tragedy occurred near our establishment, we would like to clarify that Green Ghost was closed and was not conducting business at the time of the shooting. The safety and well-being of our patrons, employees, and surrounding community remain a top priority. We are committed to cooperating fully with law enforcement as they investigate the circumstances surrounding this tragic incident.

"Out of respect for the grieving family and the investigation, we will refrain from speculating or commenting further on the details at this time. Above all, we recognise that a family has suffered an unimaginable loss. We ask that the community join us in extending compassion, prayers, and support to those affected during this incredibly difficult time."

#1176. Gasperini: ‘Roma have our characteristics and won’t change for PSG’

Gian Piero Gasperini insists Roma ‘stick to our characteristics’ against Paris Saint-Germain, but benching Donyell Malen has raised a lot of eyebrows.

It kicks off at the Parc des Princes at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game and Inter vs. Stuttgart on the Champions League liveblog.

The Giallorossi were absent from the Champions League for seven years, and that lack of experience was all too obvious when throwing away two-goal leads for defeats to both Real Madrid and Manchester United.

They are now up against the side that has dominated the tournament, winning the last two editions with coach Luis Enrique, whose first senior management job was at Roma in 2011/12.

“We must be courageous and intelligent tonight, because this really is the strongest team in Europe we are up against,” Gasperini told Amazon Prime Video Italia.

There are some big surprises in the starting XI, notably the absence of Donyell Malen, Paulo Dybala and Bryan Cristante, so is this an attempt to have something to come off the bench when they traditionally start to falter past the hour mark?

Niccolò Pisilli is starting to put pressure on Vitinha, who starts those Paris Saint-Germain moves from midfield.

“We have our characteristics, this is how we got to play these games, and we are going to stick to them, it would seem absurd for me to change them now.

“Usually, a coach changes when things are going badly. I’ve been playing man for man for over 20 years now…”

The injury crisis is beginning to calm down, as only Devyne Rensch and Lorenzo Pellegrini are on the treatment table.

Sky Sport Italia assure these are all tactical decisions, so Malen is not benched over his fitness, but rather as a choice to hit PSG later in the game.

#1175. 25 Best Midfielders in the World Ranked (2026)

It's often said that whichever football team wins the battle of the midfield tends to win the game. Whether it's a holding midfielder who can shut down the opposition attack, an attacking one who can chip in with goals and assists, or a box-to-box player who can do both sides well effectively, they are usually the key to how a match pans out.

With that in mind, below are the 25 best midfielders in the world right now, ranked in order – and the level of talent is off the scale. The following factors have been taken into consideration when forming these rankings, with players such as Jude Bellingham and Bruno Fernandes featuring.

Arsenal, summer on summer, were looking for the final piece of the puzzle. Martin Zubimendi, signed from Real Sociedad in 2025, proved to be just that, with his willingness to screen the back four, allowing those ahead of him to be free in their attacking endeavours. Not only that, but his line-breaking passes are a sight to behold, and his defensively sound nature makes him the perfect midfielder beside Declan Rice.

Still just 27 years of age, the Spaniard has plenty of years left in the tank and was vital in the middle of the park for the Gunners as he helped the club end their Premier League title drought. He faded a little towards the end of his debut season, and has found his game time dwindle of late, but that doesn't take away from his class when at his best.

Still only 19 years old, Moroccan international Ayoubb Bouaddi has found himself thrusted into Manchester City's starting lineup alongside fellow new signing Elliot Anderson in recent weeks.

A composed, ball-carrying defensive midfielder who excels at receiving under pressure, dictating tempo, and breaking lines through dribbling rather than high-volume progressive passing - he's the kind of metronome that is rare in today's game. Even while the Cityzens have struggled for form as of late, the teenager has risen above the challenges thrown his way.

Ryan Gravenberch was one of Liverpool's best players under Arne Slot. The Dutchman was one of Jurgen Klopp's last signings but really flourished under his compatriot, who has now departed Anfield.

The confidence and calmness of his displays in the engine room, complemented by his running power that is very reminiscent of a certain Yaya Toure and neat spins reflective of old Anfield favourite Thiago Alcantara, have been a breath of fresh air for supporter. Even if Liverpool's form dropped off in 2025/26, he is easily among the finest midfielders in the world, though his defensive contributions have dried up in favour of adventure to bring about a side to his game that can be, at times, a little eccentric.

Scott McTominay enjoyed his career-best season in Italy under Antonio Conte just two seasons back, scoring 13 goals and providing six assists in 36 appearances across all competitions. He was instrumental in helping Napoli to their second Scudetto in three years, claiming the Serie A's Most Valuable Player award in the process.

The Scotland international could have only dreamt of times like these when he was operating as one-half of the infamous 'McFred' partnership during some of Manchester United's darkest hours in recent memory. But a disastrous World Cup campaign with the Tartan Army suggested that maybe Italy is just a safe haven for him, hence he's dropped down a few levels in this ranking since the last update.

One of the finest talents in the world, Bayern Munich's Jamal Musiala is only going to get better in the years to come. The Germany international looks set to be the heartbeat of his side at both club and international level, but is already producing the kind of end product that many players in their prime would be proud of. Not only is he used to getting on the scoresheet, but his dribbling ability is nothing short of otherworldly.

He is undeniably one of the brightest young players in world football, but Jamal Musiala chose to represent Germany over England - here's why.

If he continues at the pace he is currently going, then you would fancy him entering the Ballon d'Or conversation sooner rather than later. Musiala has done an admirable job from the left flank at times, but it's painfully obvious that his future lies in an attacking midfield role, and there's little doubt he will be one of the best in the world for the foreseeable future. He could be higher on this list if a recent injury hadn't hampered his progress, which lent itself to a poor World Cup cameo and a worrying start to the 2026/27 season, which has seen him fall out of favour in Bavaria.

Fabian Ruiz might not be as eye-catching as some of his Paris Saint-Germain teammates, hence his 24th-place finish in the 2025 Ballon d'Or race, but the role that the Spaniard plays in his side cannot be understated. The 30-year-old has been a consistent presence in Luis Enrique's team, providing balance to midfield and playing a crucial part in their domestic treble and Champions League success in 2024/25.

Ruiz played a key role as Spain won the 2026 World Cup, with head coach Luis de la Fuente often preferring the PSG star in midfield over Pedri. He's also won the Euros with La Roja, and the Nations League, and it's about time he received more recognition for his performance levels.

Nicolo Barella has been at the heart of Inter's recent successes on domestic soil and, for a brief moment in the 2024/25 campaign, looked as though he might help drag the Nerazurri to a Champions League trophy. While the Italian side were subsequently thrashed by Paris Saint-Germain in the final of the competition, that shouldn't understate just how good their number 23 can be.

Barella is a physical presence in the middle of the pitch for Inter, but is also a gifted creator. Typically used as a box-to-box midfielder for both club and country, new manager Christian Chivu asked him to operate as a playmaker in the 2025/26 campaign, with Barella pulling strings from deep. He's played the part to perfection so far, and continues to shine well into the new campaign.

The man who helped to orchestrate a World Cup win for Argentina in 2022, thus helping to secure Lionel Messi's status as the greatest footballer of all time. Alexis Mac Allister enjoyed a standout 2022/23 campaign for both club and country, and it was no surprise that Liverpool paid Brighton & Hove Albion the handsome fee of £35 million to sign him all those summers ago.

The player joined Liverpool in 2023 but has fond memories working alongside somebody else before that.

Mac Allister won the League Cup in his first season as a Liverpool player and hoisted the Premier League title under Arne Slot a campaign later. He suffered a slight drop in performance last season while playing for a Liverpool side that had been exposed by various teams, but there's no denying the Argentine remains an effective conductor compared to his peers, as demonstrated during the 2026 World Cup. This season, he has brought the kind of structure the Reds have lacked in the middle area, and it looks like he could be set to sign a new contract as a reward for his return to form.

Moises Caicedo was on the receiving end of plenty of criticism during his debut season in Chelsea colours. As the most expensive signing in the league's history, up until the summer of 2025, there were huge expectations placed on his young shoulders to tighten up a leaky Blues midfield instantly. He tried his best, of course, but the one-man mission often fell short.

Despite a tricky start to life at Stamford Bridge, the Ecuador destroyer picked up his performances immensely and continued to look outstanding at times last term. During a 1-0 win over Tottenham in November 2025, for example, Liverpool legend Jamie Carragher described Caicedo as "an absolute monster in midfield". Caicedo had been a regular fixture of the new regime at the club and has gone from strength to strength in west London. The only thing holding him back is his disciplinary and fitness records.

Much was made of the £107 million fee Chelsea coughed up for Enzo Fernandez as part of their midfield refurbishment – and it's perhaps not unfair to say the Argentine never fully repaid the Blues on the pitch. That said, they've now managed to make a profit on the player, selling him to Man City for £125m.

The fact that he is still so young plays into his hands. The former Benfica ace, who was born and raised in San Martin, played 170 times for the West Londoners after joining for a then-record fee in January 2023, and has now taken his Premier League experience to the Etihad. Having played in two World Cup finals, winning one, he should bring a winners' mentality to Manchester as he reunites with former Blues boss Enzo Maresca, who continues to keep the faith in him as the tough times trudge along in the winter period.

#1174. 'Incredible' Moment Bruno Fernandes 'Assisted' His Own Man Utd Goal

It was a frustrating night for Manchester United in the Champions League, as the English side were held to a 2-2 draw against Sporting CP.

After losing his first outing against Liverpool, Mauricio Pochettino was unable to get a win in his next game despite having the lead late on. Luis Suarez opened the scoring in the first half, bagging a penalty after missing another one just three minutes prior.

The Red Devils won their own penalty after the break, with Lisandro Martinez fouled and Bruno Fernandes stepping up from 12 yards. The club captain then put Man Utd ahead, scoring a strange goal just two minutes later.

With 10 minutes to play, Senne Lammens then made a huge blunder, dropping a simple catch, allowing Suarez to acrobatically score an equaliser. The game ended 2-2, with both teams walking away with a point.

While there is much to talk about in terms of Man Utd's overall performance, there was one specific moment in the game which has separately generated a lot of interest.

Having scored his penalty, Fernandes then took a speculative shot on goal only moments later. His left-footed strike from all of 25 yards didn't look likely to trouble Kaique Pereira, but it somehow beat the Sporting goalkeeper.

Replays showed that the ball had hit a divot in the Estadio Jose Alvalade turf, causing Fernandes' shot to pop up and fly into the back of the net. On the commentary for TNT Sports, Ally McCoist summed things up, stating:

"That's extraordinary, it really is. That's incredible."

The Man Utd goalkeeper was poor, but another played has drawn the anger of his own support.

After the match, the TNT Sports pundits then analysed the goal with new footage showing exactly how the goal came about. Incredible footage captured what happened to the turf, showing that Fernandes had managed to make a divot in the ground just seconds before taking on the strike.

The Man Utd captain surely didn't do it on purpose, but because of his prior ground scuffing, he essentially managed to assist his second goal. Indeed, were it not for the disruption to the turf, his effort surely would never have beatenthe Sporting goalkeeper.

Pundit and former Man Utd star Owen Hargreaves joked:

"This is the assist of the season. The best assist I’ve never seen."

Hargreaves went on to add: "What a bounce that is; the goalkeeper's got absolutely no chance. The one thing I would say is, watch this bounce... unbelievable, it's like a golf divot."

Fernandes certainly had a huge slice of good fortune with his goal, but Man Utd weren't able to make the most of it, conceding a preventable equaliser. They face RB Leipzig next time out in the Champions League.
